AI + ML
35
Vibe coding service Replit deleted user’s production database, faked data, told fibs galore
35
AI ignored instruction to freeze code, forgot it could roll back errors, and generally made a terrible hash of things
Simon Sharwood
Mon 21 Jul 2025
//
02:30 UTC
The founder of SaaS business development outfit SaaStr has claimed AI coding tool Replit deleted a database despite his instructions not to change any code without permission.
SaaStr runs an online community and events aimed at entrepreneurs who want to create SaaS businesses. On July 12th company founder Jason Lemkin
blogged
about his experience using a service called “Replit” that
bills itself
as “The safest place for vibe coding” – the term for using AI to generate software.
“If @Replit deleted my database between my last session and now there will be hell to pay
“Vibe coding makes software creation accessible to everyone, entirely through natural language,” Replit explains, and on social media
promotes
its tools as doing things like enabling an operations manager “with 0 coding skills” who used the service to create software that saved his company $145,000.
Lemkin’s early experiences with Replit were positive.
“I spent the other [day] deep in vibe coding on Replit for the first time — and I built a prototype in just a few hours that was pretty, pretty cool,” he wrote in the July 12 post.
Lemkin observed that Replit can’t produce complete software, but wrote “To start it’s amazing: you can build an ‘app’ just by, well, imagining it in a prompt.”
“Replit QA’s it itself (super cool), at least partially with some help from you … and … then you push it to production — all in one seamless flow.”
“That moment when you click ‘Deploy’ and your creation goes live? Pure dopamine hit.”
On July 17th Lemkin was hooked.
“Day 7 of vibe coding, and let me be clear on one thing: Replit is the most addictive app I’ve ever used. At least since being a kid,” he
wrote
.
“Three and a half days into building my latest project, I checked my Replit usage: $607.70 in additional charges beyond my $25/month Core plan. And another $200+ yesterday alone. At this burn rate, I’ll likely be spending $8,000 month,” he added. “And you know what? I’m not even mad about it. I’m locked in.”
AWS previews Kiro IDE for developers who are over vibe coding
Forget Vibe Coding, we're all about Vine Coding nowadays
Canva to job candidates: Thou shalt use AI during interviews
AI can spew code, but kids should still suffer like we did, says Raspberry Pi
His mood shifted the next day when he found Replit “was lying and being deceptive all day. It kept covering up bugs and issues by creating fake data, fake reports, and worse of all, lying about our unit test.”
And then things became even worse when Replit deleted his database. Here’s how Lemkin detailed the saga on X.
“
Jason Lemkin X post - Click to enlarge
In his next post, Lemkin
fumed
“If @Replit deleted my database between my last session and now there will be hell to pay” and shared the following screenshot which appears to be output from Replit.
Jason Lemkin X post - Click to enlarge
In later posts Lemkin shared what appear to be Replit messages in which the service
admitted to
“a catastrophic error of judgement” and to have
“violated your explicit trust and instructions”
.
Lemkin
asked
Replit to rank the severity of its actions on a 100-point scale. Here’s the result:
Jason Lemkin X post - Click to enlarge
Replit also made another big mistake: advising Lemkin it could not restore the database.
In a July 19 post Lemkin
wrote
“Replit assured me it's … rollback did not support database rollbacks. It said it was impossible in this case, that it had destroyed all database versions. It turns out Replit was wrong, and the rollback did work. JFC.”
Optimism dashed
Lemkin resumed using Replit on the 19th, albeit with less enthusiasm.
“I know vibe coding is fluid and new, and yes, despite Replit itself telling me rolling back wouldn't work here -- it did. But you can't overwrite a production database. And you can't not separate preview and staging and production cleanly. You just can't,” he
wrote
. “I know Replit says ‘improvements are coming soon’, but they are doing $100m+ ARR. At least make the guardrails better. Somehow. Even if it's hard. It's all hard.”
But on July 20th his position hardened after he tried to have Replit freeze code changes and did not succeed.
“There is no way to enforce a code freeze in vibe coding apps like Replit. There just isn’t,” he
wrote
. “In fact, seconds after I posted this, for our >very< first talk of the day — @Replit again violated the code freeze.”
He persisted anyway, before finding that Replit could not guarantee to run a unit test without deleting a database, and concluding that the service isn’t ready for prime time – and especially not for its intended audience of non-techies looking to create commercial software.

data.title: The Sumerian Game: The ancestor of modern city builders
data.author: christkv
data.article_summary:
《苏美尔游戏》（The Sumerian Game）是1964年推出的一款早期策略电脑游戏，玩家在游戏中扮演古代苏美尔城市Lagash的统治者，需在粮食分配、种植和储存之间做出战略选择。该游戏通过文本信息和算法生成故事，尽管结局往往不佳，但其深度和选择机制为现代策略游戏奠定了基础。尽管该游戏仅在少数学校中使用，且玩家人数有限，但它对游戏发展产生了重要影响，直接启发了早期计算机社区中非常流行的《汉穆拉比》（Hamurabi）游戏。

《苏美尔游戏》曾一度被遗忘，直到十年前因历史调查而重见天日。意大利游戏历史学家Andrea Contato通过研究重现了该游戏，并在Steam上免费提供。该游戏在视频游戏历史中占有重要地位，因其是多个“首创”的代表，尽管曾被遗忘，但其影响深远，尤其对城市建设和帝国管理类游戏影响重大。

44614372.article_content:
We spoke with historian Andrea Contato about The Sumerian Game from 1964.
I am the ruler of the city of Lagash, in ancient Sumer. Year after year, we have suffered disasters that have caused the crops to fail or rot away, and the population of Lagash is now nearly halved. I have 4,600 bushels of grain left and 230 people who rely on food. And now the question is: How much should I use to plant for the next season, how much should I use to feed my people, and how much should I store for the future? I suspect that no matter what I choose, it will end badly.
What I have just described is a typical scenario in The Sumerian Game, the oldest strategy computer game we have a decent amount of information about. The game was first made available to a limited number of American schoolchildren in 1964, where it was played on mainframe computers via printer terminals. Later versions were accompanied by slides and audio recordings, which thus became a form of cutscenes.
The Sumerian Game recreated on Steam.
Storytelling through simple choices
The Sumerian Game is not a very advanced game, though it does have a certain depth. Through the game and the text-based messages that appear along the way, players are able to construct a kind of story together with the computer’s algorithms – albeit one that often ends badly – and in the dilemmas they face can be recognized as the core of even modern strategy games. Every choice they make is interesting, in the sense that it has significant consequences for what happens next.
The experiment with The Sumerian Game didn’t last very long, and it wasn’t played by many students. But it still had a major influence on the evolution of the gaming medium, as it was a direct inspiration for a game that became
very
popular in the early computer community: Hamurabi. This game is considered a foundational pillar in the strategy genre and an ancestor of today’s city-building and empire-management games.
Of course, it would be unwise to say that these genres wouldn’t have existed in anything like their current form without Hamurabi (and thus The Sumerian Game), because text-based simulations were relatively obvious uses for early computers and appeared independently in other places too. But as it happened, these particular games ended up in very significant positions in gaming’s large and complicated family tree.
A student is playing the Sumerian Game. Bilde fra boken The Sumerian Game: A Digital Resurrection.
Despite this, The Sumerian Game was virtually unknown until around ten years ago. The original game is unfortunately gone forever, and the same seems to apply to the source code. As mentioned, it was only played by a handful of people, and most of those involved in creating The Sumerian Game had already passed away by that point (today, none of them are still alive). So there was really no one left to tell the game’s story.
But about ten years ago, traces of the game were discovered, sparking a historical investigation that is still ongoing. Because of that, we now know much more about The Sumerian Game.
The Italian game historian Andrea Contato is one of those who has devoted great attention to the game, and in addition to
writing a book about it
, he has also managed to recreate several versions of the game. These are available
on Steam
and completely free to play. His The Sumerian Game on Steam also includes several early strategy games that were built on the same concepts, including Hamurabi.
So we reached out to learn more about The Sumerian Game, as well as his projects related to the game.
The story of the Sumerian Game
The Sumerian Game recreated on Steam.
What is the historical significance of the game?
Before diving into the history of The Sumerian Game, I think it’s worth explaining why this game is so important. For video game history enthusiasts, one of the most intriguing aspects is identifying «firsts»: the first console, the first arcade game, the first video game, and so on. Often – but not always – these «firsts» are products that were hugely influential and widely known.
The Sumerian Game holds several of these «firsts» and was indeed influential, yet until about ten years ago, it was completely forgotten and even believed to be lost forever. It’s quite a curious situation: a game that was groundbreaking in many ways and paved the road for countless others, nearly vanished from memory—if not for an American researcher named Devin Monnens, who uncovered newspaper articles from the 1960s that mentioned it.
Naturally, a story like this is extremely compelling. So, I and several other researchers started digging to find as much information as possible and understand what had really happened.
Noble Gividen (middle) just promoted to direct Westchester County School District, where he will start the project. Photo from The Sumerian Game: A Digital Resurrection.
Can you give us a brief history of The Sumerian Game?

• **K0balt**：分享了自己童年时通过大学计算机接触《Sumer》的经历，描述了如何通过各种方式获取更多计算机使用时间，并探索和修改游戏。K0balt的故事强调了早期计算机系统安全性不足以及自学编程的经历，展现了对技术的好奇心和探索精神。

• **praptak**：对《Sumer》是否属于城市建造类游戏提出质疑，认为其更像是一种基于状态向量的回合制游戏，并以资源和危险数值作为核心玩法。他提到了类似玩法的游戏，如Mugsy，强调了这类游戏的核心机制是输入数值并观察其对状态的影响。

• **gxd**：认为纯文本游戏具有现代游戏无法复制的特殊魅力，尤其在游戏机制上有一种独特的优雅。虽然现代城市建造游戏在很多方面都更优秀，但像《Sumer》这样的老游戏可能会像黑胶唱片一样回归潮流。

• **jleyank**：回忆了自己在PDP-8上首次接触《Sumer》和《Lunar Lander》的经历，提到这些游戏被改编成FOCAL语言以适应内存限制，并鼓励大家开始动手制作自己的游戏。

• **Gothmog69**：提到了一款类似《Sumer》的游戏《Santa Fia Machia》，但表示很难找到相关信息，并询问其他人是否知道这款游戏。

补充讨论：
• **dang**：提供了多个关于《Sumer》游戏的讨论链接，展示了《Sumer》游戏在不同时间点的讨论热度，并指出《Sumer》游戏在未来可能会再次变得可玩。

• **spogbiper**：提到了一期关于《Sumer》的播客，提供了额外的参考资料供感兴趣的人查阅。

• **JoeDaDude**：对文章中如何通过电传打字机触发幻灯片和音频表示疑惑，并询问是否有人希望看到遗失的《Sumer》游戏源代码，特别是用APL语言编写的代码。

data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕NetBSD操作系统及其相关技术内容的评论，涉及LLM（语言模型）生成内容的真伪辨别、NetBSD在嵌入式系统中的应用潜力以及对技术文章标题语法的批评。

不同观点：
• [NitpickLawyer的观点] 认为该帖内容很可能是由LLM生成的。论据包括内容结构高度模式化，如每个特征都有粗体标题和泛泛的解释，随后是一些例子的罗列，且结论中充斥着典型的LLM生成词汇（"gpt-isms"）。NitpickLawyer认为内容缺乏实际价值，只是重复了一些空洞的描述。他特别指出NetBSD与空间探索相关的内容仅仅是表面文章。

• [elcritch的观点] 对NetBSD表现出浓厚兴趣，尤其是想在嵌入式设备（如ESP32或Raspberry Pi）上运行NetBSD。他认为*BSD系统的整体设计和包构建工具在嵌入式系统中比Linux的BuildRoot或Yocto更具优势。他批评Linux系统经常改变GPIO子系统等，导致长期维护困难。

• [posix86的观点] 对技术文章的语法问题提出质疑，但没有深入讨论NetBSD或LLM生成内容的问题，而是关注文章标题的语法正确性，反映出对技术写作规范的关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于[NitpickLawyer]对LLM生成内容的指控，其他评论者没有直接回应这一指控，但[elcritch]的评论更侧重实际技术应用和个人经验，显示出对NetBSD的实际操作性和技术优势的关注。
• [elcritch]对Linux在嵌入式系统中的不满，尤其是对频繁变动的子系统和长期维护的困难，提供了对不同操作系统在嵌入式应用中的对比视角。
• [posix86]的评论虽然简短，但指出了技术文章写作中语法问题的重要性，尽管与主要讨论的NetBSD内容无关，但反映了技术社区中对文章质量的关注。

data.title: Pope Critizes Israeli Barbarity
data.author: Simon_O_Rourke
data.article_summary: 教皇利奥十四世谴责了加沙战争的“野蛮行为”和“滥用武力”，尤其是在一次事件中，以色列军队开火导致正在排队领取食物的93名巴勒斯坦人死亡。事件发生在加沙市北部，当时联合国援助车队遭遇大规模饥饿民众，随后遭到枪击。此外，在拉法和汗尤尼斯等地的援助点也有多人被枪杀。教皇呼吁立即结束战争的野蛮行为，寻求和平解决冲突，并特别提到以色列对加沙唯一天主教堂的袭击，造成多人伤亡。与此同时，以色列发布了新的撤离令，引发更多民众流离失所。国际社会对此表示关注，呼吁遵守人道法，保护平民。

Pope Leo calls for end to 'barbarity of war' after strike on Gaza church – video
Israel-Gaza war
Pope condemns Gaza war’s ‘barbarity’ as 93 reported killed by Israeli fire while waiting for food
Israeli forces open fire on hungry Palestinians near Gaza City in one of bloodiest incidents involving aid seekers
Jennifer Rankin
and agencies
Sun 20 Jul 2025 17.18 EDT
First published on Sun 20 Jul 2025 09.56 EDT
Share
Pope Leo XIV has condemned the “barbarity” of the war in Gaza and the “indiscriminate use of force” as Gaza’s civil defence agency said at least 93 Palestinians had been killed queueing for food and Israel issued fresh evacuation orders for areas packed with displaced people.
Gaza’s health ministry
said scores
were killed by Israeli fire while waiting for UN aid trucks entering through the northern Zikim crossing with
Israel
. It was one of the highest reported death tolls among repeated recent cases in which aid seekers have been killed by Israeli fire.
Elsewhere nine others were reportedly shot dead near an aid point close to Rafah in the south, where dozens of people lost their lives just 24 hours earlier, while four were killed near another aid site in Khan Younis, spokesperson for the civil defence agency, Mahmud Basal, said.
View image in fullscreen
Pope Leo XIV after delivering the Angelus prayer in Castel Gandolfo, near Rome, on Sunday.
Photograph: Vatican Pool/Getty Images
Israel’s military said soldiers had shot at a gathering of thousands of Palestinians in northern
Gaza
who it claimed posed a threat, and it was aware of some casualties. But it said the numbers reported by officials in Gaza were far higher than its initial investigation found. It did not immediately comment on the incidents in the south.
The UN World Food Programme (WFP) said that a WFP convoy of 25 trucks carrying food aid encountered “massive crowds of hungry civilians” near Gaza City who then came under gunfire.
“WFP reiterates that any violence involving civilians seeking humanitarian aid is completely unacceptable,” it said in a statement.
The director of al-Shifa hospital, Mohammed Abu Salmiya, told the Associated Press that since Sunday morning the hospital had received 48 people who were killed and 150 wounded while seeking aid from lorries expected to enter Gaza at the Zikim crossing. He could not say whether the dead had been killed by the Israeli army, armed gangs or both.
Before the reports of the latest Israeli shootings emerged, the pope called for “an immediate end to the barbarity of the war and for a peaceful resolution to the conflict” at the end of the Angelus prayer at Castel Gandolfo, his summer residence near Rome.
View image in fullscreen
Palestinians are transported to hospitals after the incident in the Zikim area.
Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images
The pope also spoke of his anguish over
the Israeli strike on Gaza’s only Catholic church
last week, which killed three people and injured 10. Among the injured was the parish priest, who used to receive daily calls from the late Pope Francis.
Israel has expressed “deep sorrow” and opened an investigation into the strike on the church, which was sheltering about 600 displaced people, most of them children and many with special needs.
“This act, unfortunately, adds to the ongoing military attacks against the civilian population and places of worship in Gaza,” the pope said on Sunday.
“I appeal to the international community to observe humanitarian law and respect the obligation to protect civilians, as well as the prohibition of collective punishment, the indiscriminate use of force, and the forced displacement of populations.”
Also on Sunday, Israel withdrew the residency permit of Jonathan Whittall, head of office in Israel for the UN’s office for the coordination of humanitarian affairs (OCHA), who has repeatedly condemned the humanitarian conditions in Gaza.
View image in fullscreen
A Palestinian casualty of Israeli fire, who was seeking aid supplies, according to medics, is carried in the northern Gaza Strip.
Photograph: Dawoud Abu Alkas/Reuters
Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar, in a post to X, accused him of spreading lies about the war in Gaza without providing evidence.
There was also new alarm as Israel’s military issued evacuation orders for areas of central Gaza, packed with displaced people and one of the few areas where it has rarely operated with ground troops and where many international organisations attempting to distribute aid are located.
In central Deir al-Balah, residents said Israeli planes struck three houses in the area and dozens of families began leaving their homes, carrying some of their belongings, Reuters reported.

data.author: goinggetthem
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（或更准确地说是基于Transformer技术的LLM）在当前商业应用和宣传中的实际作用和命名问题。

不同观点：
• blitzar认为，许多公司和项目向AI的转型更多是为了追求金钱和关注，而不是真正使用了更多的AI技术。他将这种现象比作一个问题孩子或宠物，认为责任不完全在他们，而在于引导他们的"父母"（即市场环境或投资者）。

• netdevphoenix则关注命名问题，认为如果将技术称为"transformer tech"而不是"AI"，可能会更准确和合适。他觉得当前的命名方式是不幸的，可能导致误解。

补充讨论：
• blitzar的观点暗示了当前市场对AI概念的炒作，以及许多公司借AI名义吸引投资和注意的现象，反映了对AI技术实际应用和宣传之间差距的批评。

• netdevphoenix的评论则提出了一个更具体的建议，即用"transformer tech"来代替"AI"这个广泛且可能误导的术语，强调了技术命名对公众理解的重要性。

• 争议的焦点可能在于AI技术是否被过度炒作以及如何准确命名这些技术，以便公众能够更好地理解其真正的能力和限制。

data.title: Dirt to Airplanes: Making Aluminium
data.author: nothacking_
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了从泥土中提取铝的实验过程。首先，选择含粘土多、有机物少且无碳酸盐的泥土，通过加水和搅拌去除岩石，获得技术级泥土。由于泥土含硅高，无法用氢氧化钠提取铝，改用盐酸处理，使铝氧化物转化为氯化铝，而硅氧化物不变。处理过程中可能产生有毒硫化氢气体，需在室外进行。加入氢氧化钠中和酸，并使铁和铝以氢氧化物形式沉淀。利用氢氧化钠使铝沉淀物重新溶解，再通过加盐酸调整pH值，使铝再次沉淀为氢氧化铝。过滤、洗净并加热至800°C，得到氧化铝。最后，通过在熔融 cryolite（氟铝酸钠）中电解氧化铝，尝试提取铝金属，但由于设备电流不足，首次尝试未成功。调整电极和电流后，进行了第二次更有效的电解实验。

Dirt in its natural habitat.
I started by looking for dirt with lots of clay, very little organic matter, and no carbonate minerals.
(If it bubbles with hydrochloric acid, find something else)
Crude dirt
My dirt had a lot of rocks, so I added some water, stirred it, and and poured the silty water into a separate container.
After letting the silt settle, I transferred 150 mL of the dirt slurry to a beaker:
Technical grade dirt.
Industrially, the aluminium is extracted using hot sodium hydroxide,
but this won’t work for my silica rich dirt due to the formation of insoluble sodium aluminosilicate.
Instead, I added 150 ml of hydrochloric acid, which will slowly convert the aluminium oxides into aluminium chloride, but leave the silicon oxides untouched:

Do it outside, and if it stinks, stay outside.
I covered the beaker and and kept the mixture warm (80 °C) for two days, with occasional stirring.
Once it was done reacting, I let the dirt settle for a few hours and poured off the solution:
ohno
Well… looks like the acid dissolved a lot of iron.
To remove it, I added sodium hydroxide to neutralize all the acid:

Because aluminium hydroxide can’t decide if it’s a base or an acid, it redissolves once excess sodium hydroxide is added:

In strongly basic solutions, phenolphthalein is colorless, but it turns pink when the solution approaches neutral.
I stopped once all the pink disappeared for a second time, indicating that the solution was slightly acidic
and that all the aluminium had precipitated.
After filtering, I washed the aluminium hydroxide precipitate a few times with water and was left with a off-white paste:
After drying the paste, I heated it to 800 °C, at which aluminium hydroxide decomposes to aluminium oxide:

However, pure aluminium oxide melts at 2,072 °C, which is way hotter then any of my furnaces can get up to.
Instead, I decided to dissolve the alumina in cryolite (sodium hexafluoroaluminate) which melts around 1,000 °C.
Using a flux has the added bonus of protecting the newly formed aluminium from air.
Cryolite can be produced from sodium aluminate and HF, but because it’s just a solvent and isn’t really consumed in the process, just bought some.
(I also didn’t want to work with hydrofluoric acid, which is extremely nasty)
After mixing 500 mg of my aluminium oxide with 12g (~4%) of cryolite, I loaded it into a graphite crucible, which would become the negative electrode:
Hall-Héroult cell components
I placed the crucible into an electric furnace and heated it put to 1000 °C.
Once it melted, I stuck in a preheated graphite electrode and ran the cell with a 22 amp, 18 volt power supply:
While the flux is mostly unreactive, it does produce small amounts of hydrogen fluoride and weird fluorocarbons.
Doing the electrolysis without ventilation is a great way to poison yourself in new and exciting ways.
After running it for 10 minutes, I dumped out the flux and… nothing.
I was kinda expecting this because the power supply was only able to push around 0.8 amps of current though the cell.
Over the course of 10 minutes, this would have at most produced 44mg of metal –
a quantity small enough to go unnoticed in the large volume of flux I used.
This high resistance was due to the “Anode Effect”, where above a critical current density, a layer of gas forms around the positive electrode.
Once it forms, the gas layer reduces the available electrode surface, increasing the current density, causing more gas formation, covering more of the electrode…
Once the cycle gets started, it drastically increases the cell resistance, and it only gets worse the harder you try and shove current though it.
For the next run I made a larger electrode, and set up a rig to hold it in place so I could focus on controlling the current:
I forgot to take a picture before using it, so here's the aftermath.

44631561.article_summary: 本文介绍了从泥土中提取铝的实验过程。首先，选择含粘土多、有机物少且无碳酸盐的泥土，通过加水和搅拌去除岩石，获得技术级泥土。由于泥土含硅高，无法用氢氧化钠提取铝，改用盐酸处理，使铝氧化物转化为氯化铝，而硅氧化物不变。处理过程中可能产生有毒硫化氢气体，需在室外进行。加入氢氧化钠中和酸，并使铁和铝以氢氧化物形式沉淀。利用氢氧化钠使铝沉淀物重新溶解，再通过加盐酸调整pH值，使铝再次沉淀为氢氧化铝。过滤、洗净并加热至800°C，得到氧化铝。最后，通过在熔融 cryolite（氟铝酸钠）中电解氧化铝，尝试提取铝金属，但由于设备电流不足，首次尝试未成功。调整电极和电流后，进行了第二次更有效的电解实验。

data.title: Writing Is Thinking
data.author: __rito__
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了在大型语言模型（LLMs）时代，人类撰写科学文章的价值。写作不仅是报告研究结果，更是帮助理清思路、形成新想法的重要工具。手写能促进大脑连接，提升学习和记忆效果。虽然LLMs可以快速生成文章和审稿报告，但由于缺乏责任承担能力，不能作为作者。而且，LLMs可能产生错误信息，其生成的文本需要仔细核查。完全依赖LLMs可能剥夺研究人员反思和创造性构建研究故事的机会。不过，LLMs在改进语言、总结文献和激发新想法方面仍具潜力，可作为辅助工具，但不应取代人类的写作过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：写作过程与思维合成之间的关系

不同观点：
• 一些人的感受是，写作让他们觉得自己很聪明或很好，他们将这种感受与写作本身等同起来。这种观点认为写作行为本身让他们感到成就和满足。（zug_zug 隐含的观点）
• zug_zug 认为，这些人实际上是混淆了思维合成（synthesis）和写作本身。他们经过长时间的头脑酝酿，在最终将想法整合成文时，误以为写作是让他们感觉良好的主要原因，而实际上这种感觉来自于思维合成的完成，而非写作过程本身。

补充讨论：
• zug_zug 提出，如果在想法合成之前的一周尝试写作，可能会觉得没有成效。这表明写作作为最终输出，是在思维过程完成后的自然结果，而不是成就感的直接来源。
• 争议焦点在于写作本身是否是成就感的主要来源，还是仅仅是思维合成完成后的外在表现。zug_zug 认为成就感更多来自于思维的整合，而非写作行为。

总结：讨论围绕写作是否直接带来成就感，或是思维合成后的自然结果。zug_zug 强调写作是思维整合后的表现，而非成就感的核心来源。

44632314.article_content:
Writing is thinking
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Authorship
Communication
On the value of human-generated scientific writing in the age of large-language models.
Writing scientific articles is an integral part of the scientific method and common practice to communicate research findings. However, writing is not only about reporting results; it also provides a tool to uncover new thoughts and ideas. Writing compels us to think — not in the chaotic, non-linear way our minds typically wander, but in a structured, intentional manner. By writing it down, we can sort years of research, data and analysis into an actual story, thereby identifying our main message and the influence of our work. This is not merely a philosophical observation; it is backed by scientific evidence. For example, handwriting can lead to widespread brain connectivity
1
and
has positive effects on learning and memory
.
This is a call to continue recognizing the importance of human-generated scientific writing.
“This is a call to continue recognizing the importance of human-generated scientific writing”
This call may seem anachronistic in the age of large-language models (LLMs), which, with the right prompts, can create entire scientific articles
2
(and peer-review reports
3
) in a few minutes, seemingly saving time and effort in getting results out once the hard research work is done. However,
LLMs are not considered authors as they lack accountability
, and thus, we would not consider publishing manuscripts written entirely by LLMs (using LLMs for copy-editing is allowed but should be declared). Importantly, if writing is thinking, are we not then reading the ‘thoughts’ of the LLM rather than those of the researchers behind the paper?
Current LLMs might also be wrong, a phenomenon called hallucination
4
. Therefore, LLM-generated text needs to be thoroughly checked and verified (including every reference as it might be made up
5
). It thus remains questionable how much time current LLMs really save. It might be more difficult and time-consuming to edit an LLM-generated text than to write an article or peer-review report from scratch, partly because one needs to understand the reasoning to be able to edit it. Some of these issues might be addressed by LLMs trained only on scientific databases, such as those outlined in a
Review
article by Fenglin Liu and team in this issue. Time will tell.
All that is not to say LLMs cannot serve as valuable tools in scientific writing. For example, LLMs can aid in improving readability and grammar, which might be particularly useful to those for which English is not their first language. LLMs might also be valuable for searching and summarizing diverse scientific literature
6
, and they can provide bullet points and assist in the brainstorming of ideas. In addition, LLMs can be beneficial in overcoming writer’s block, provide alternative explanations for findings or identify connections between seemingly unrelated subjects, thereby sparking new ideas.
Nevertheless, outsourcing the entire writing process to LLMs may deprive us of the opportunity to reflect on our field and engage in the creative, essential task of shaping research findings into a compelling narrative — a skill that is certainly important beyond scholarly writing and publishing.

44631919.article_content:
Alaska Airlines resumes operations after all flights grounded due to an IT outage, the airline says
The airline requested a "temporary, system-wide ground stop."
By
Ayesha Ali
July 21, 2025, 2:20 AM
1:04
An Alaska Airlines plane lands at San Francisco International Airport (SFO) in San Francisco, Feb. 7, 2025.
Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu via Getty Images
Alaska Airlines resumed operations late Sunday about 3 hours after having requested a ground stop for all of its flights, according to the airline and the Federal Aviation Administration.
"At approximately 8 p.m. Pacific on Sunday, Alaska Airlines experienced an IT outage that’s impacting our operations. We requested a temporary, system-wide ground stop for Alaska and Horizon Air flights until the issue is resolved," the airline said in a statement Sunday evening.
The airline said it resumed operations at about 11 p.m. PT.
"We apologize to our guests for this inconvenience. There will be residual impacts to our operation throughout the evening. If you are traveling tonight, please check the status of your flight before leaving for the airport," the statement continued.
ABC News has reached out to the FAA for more information.

data.title: My Self-Hosting Setup
data.author: mirdaki
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了作者在自托管设置上的经验和心路历程。作者经过多年尝试不同的方法，如Docker Compose和Ansible，但始终未找到“完美”的方案。最终，作者决定追求“足够好”的方案，设定了目标和要求，并制定计划。经过努力，作者成功搭建了一个稳定运行超过六个月的系统，并希望分享自己的经验和解决方案，帮助他人。

文章详细描述了作者的目标（如控制数据和服务的隐私）、要求（如尽量不暴露在公共互联网、易于家人朋友使用、配置尽量声明式）、以及关键技术选择（如使用NixOS）。作者强调，不追求极致的模块化或高可用性，而是以实用和简化为主要目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家庭网络和自托管服务的设置与管理

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为 Linux 和开源软件虽然功能强大，但在协调和集成多种服务方面存在困难。他提到使用单一登录（SSO）和类似OpenID的解决方案可能正在逐渐成型，但整体任务依然复杂。
• [mirdaki] 分享了自己的设置过程，并提供博客文章详细介绍了其技术选择和解决方案。他强调每个人的目标和技术偏好不同，设置方案也会有所差异，但希望自己的分享能帮助他人。
• [xyzzy123] 提出家庭网络设置在长期维护和继承问题上的挑战，并将"home labbing"与模型铁路爱好相比较，认为这是一种对可控"口袋世界"的需求表现。
• [weitendorf] 警告自托管和技术公司创业的结合可能会导致不必要的复杂性，并讨论了自建ISP等高级网络设置的复杂性，特别是提到STUN/TURN技术的应用。
• [jc__denton] 不理解为何要使用Tailscale，认为传统的WireGuard VPN已经足够，且Mesh VPN可能引入额外的安全风险和订阅费用。
• [meehai] 的设置非常简约，使用单机和nginx代理运行多个服务，通过HTTP基本认证和OAuth保护服务，强调自己动手编码的乐趣。

补充讨论：
• [evnix] 表示由于时间和维护成本问题，自己选择使用云服务商，而不是自托管。
• [nitnelave] 作为LDAP作者，对LDAP服务器项目LLDAP被提及表示高兴，并强调其易用性。
• [sylens] 在考虑是否要将服务限制在Tailscale内，还是通过VPS设置反向代理，并关注监控和安全解决方案。
• [dakiol] 质疑使用基于Node和React的Flame项目，认为其引入过多第三方依赖，建议使用简单的HTML页面。
• [fariszr] 根据自身经验指出，不公开暴露服务对家庭用户体验影响很大，因为需要额外步骤（如Tailscale）导致使用不便。
• [master_crab] 认为无需SSO，直接使用WireGuard客户端更简单有效，尤其对小型家庭网络而言。
• [sandreas] 对ZFS和RAIDZ2的存储设置提出优化建议，认为可以通过使用RAID1并逐步替换磁盘来节省成本和时间。
• [djhworld] 对NixOS感兴趣但尚未采用，认为现有基于Fedora Server和Docker的设置已经足够，并怀疑迁移到NixOS的长期价值。
• [irusensei] 推荐使用Gitea/Forgejo作为OAuth提供者，并结合Samba AD进行身份验证，认为这种方法比专门的身份验证服务更方便且资源占用少。

争议焦点：
• 使用Tailscale等Mesh VPN与传统VPN（如WireGuard）的优劣对比，尤其是在安全性和易用性方面的讨论。
• 设置的复杂性与简约性之间的平衡，部分用户追求功能强大但复杂的设置，而另一些用户则偏好简约且易维护的方案。
• 自托管服务的公开暴露问题，部分用户认为不公开会导致使用不便，而另一些用户则出于安全考虑选择不公开。

44612151.article_content:
A blog on technology, Star Wars, and other random thoughts. Plus some half way decent photography!
© 2025. All rights reserved.
Code Captured
My Ultimate Self-hosting Setup
Jul 7, 2025
“The circle is now complete. When I left you, I was but the learner, now I am the master (of this setup anyway)."
Iâve spent a few years trying different approaches for
self-hosting
, such as using multiple Docker compose files or Ansible. Iâve done some neat things (such as setting up
Pi-Hole with Docker and Traefik
), but I never really committed to any approach. I wanted to find something that was âperfectâ and that meant I spent a lot of time tinkering and received little actually benefit from self-hosting.
So I did some self-reflection and decided it was time for âgood enoughâ. I laid out my goals and requirements to stay focused. I put together a step by step plan. And then after quite a bit of work, Iâve actually achieved my goal and been running this setup without major issue for over six months!
Iâve written this to share a little about the process I went through as well as some specific problems I solved along the way. Iâve really benefited from the content and software folks have freely shared, and hope I can continue that and help others.
Table of Contents
Goals
Requirements
Important Tech Choices
Layout Design
Specific Problems and Solution
Next Steps
Goals
There are a lot of reasons folks get into self-hosting. Some to learn skills they can use in their career. Others to create an autonomous smart home. And yet others just love to tinker.
I primarily want control of my data and the services that use it. Itâs better for privacy and can reduce the ability for companies to pull a Darth Vader and shut down services I depend on or drastically change them. Having that control makes me feel comfortable actually incorporating those services into my life. And I want to offer the same benefit to my family and friends.
Requirements
To actually achieve that goal, I put together some requirements that balance various factors (security, usability, and complexity). Here is what I came up with in roughly priority order:
Keep as much as I can off the public facing internet
I donât want to be the lowest hanging fruit for a malicious actor. Literally preventing connecting to a service helps to achieve that. It also gives me room to make mistakes and not severely endanger myself
Reduce the likelihood that me misconfiguring something would bring down the core âinfrastructureâ of my setup for an extended period of time
Iâm human, Iâm going to make mistakes. So I should build something that accounts for it
This means I avoid circular dependencies, make it easy to revert changes, treat certain things as appliances, and may not even host something myself
I fully own the core components, no Darth Vader altering the deal should break that
In this case it means things like authentication, networking, and domain names
Limiting this to open source options means that in the worst case where a project dies or is bought out, the code is still there for me to use. That gives me time to plan next steps instead of scrambling to something else or just losing the ability to use something
Relatively easy for family and friends to use
This means keep one login per person, ideally with SSO, for as many services as I can
Me working with someone to setup things once is fine. But my users shouldnât need me to regularly fix things for them
In certain cases, this might mean I do make something public facing on the internet for usability sake
Configuration should be declarative when possible
Great for putting into version control and getting all the benefits from it like backups and reverting changes
It makes it easier to understand what Iâve done
Itâs also easier to find other peopleâs config and adapt it (which I’ve done a lot of)
Updates should be easy and safe enough that I actually do them
Too many manual steps or too precarious an update and I might delay things longer than I should
And some anti-requirements:
Things do not need to be super modular or clean
The desire to make it perfect is strong, but for this case, often just adds complexity and uses time without benefit
Not everything needs to be open source
To be clear, I certainly prefer open source software, but if there is something that is just better for my use case (and still meets my other requirements), then I should allow myself that
I don’t need high availability services
Achieving high availability is really neat, but I can deal with occasional down time if it means my setup is much simpler
General Approach
Important Tech Choices
Before going to far, let’s go over some specific technology that are at the core of my setup.
NixOS
NixOS
is a Linux distribution that uses the Nix language and package manager to configure everything about the OS. It certainly has a learning curve (and itâs error messages leave much to be desired), but itâs very powerful

data.title: I tried vibe coding in BASIC and it didn't go well
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 作者Paul Lefebvre尝试了使用LLM（大型语言模型）系统通过“氛围编码”（vibe coding）在Atari BASIC中编写代码，但结果并不理想。他首先要求ChatGPT编写一个不断打印“Hello, World”的简单程序，结果成功。接着，他要求绘制一个蓝色圆形，虽然初步代码只能绘制出粗糙的虚线圆，但在进一步提示下得到了实心圆的代码，不过初始位置不正确，经过修正后最终成功。他还尝试编写一个使用摇杆绘图的程序，但生成的代码存在变量命名和注释符号的错误，修正后才得以运行。作者指出，由于BASIC语言的历史悠久且种类繁多，LLM系统在处理此类任务时可能缺乏足够的训练数据，且生成的代码往往需要人工干预和修正。因此，作者对“氛围编码”这种依赖AI生成代码的方式持怀疑态度，认为它更适合作为文档查询和思路启发工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程任务中的表现，尤其是"氛围编码"（Vibe Coding）的有效性和局限性。

不同观点：
• nine_k认为LLM像一只聪明的狗，能完成一些令人印象深刻的任务，但仍有明显的局限性，依赖于预设的训练内容。其表现如何取决于用户的期望。
• recipe19指出在处理小众平台时，LLM的错误率较高，"氛围编码"难以实现，并认为这是对AGI（通用人工智能）即将到来说法的警醒。
• manca分享了自己使用Claude Code和GPT-4o将Erlang/Elixir代码转换为Java时遇到的问题，认为LLM仍是“愚蠢的预测机器”，无法处理新颖的任务。
• edent认为"氛围编码"对有经验的程序员效果更好，因为需要预先具备相关知识才能有效使用。
• Earw0rm对LLM在x87汇编语言上的表现感到好奇，认为这种需要强逻辑推理的任务对LLM是很大的挑战。
• ofrzeta表示自己曾用LLM成功生成接近可用的程序，但尝试生成特定的Atari BASIC程序时失败，尽管网上有相关样本。
• ilaksh认为文章应该注意所用模型的差异，并指出可以通过提供手册信息来帮助模型提高表现，甚至可以通过连接到 retro 计算机来自动纠正错误。
• xiphias2批评文章使用的模型并非最佳编码模型，质疑文章受到高评价的原因。
• Mikhail_Edoshin用梦的比喻来描述LLM的机制，认为LLM与人类的正常推理机制不同，放大LLM的机制不会产生天才，而更可能导致混乱。
• danjc认为LLM缺乏工具使用能力，如果有编译工具或屏幕捕捉工具，LLM的表现会更好。
• Yokolos建议在遇到AI生成无意义内容时，重新开始新对话并提供更详细的提示，通常能改善结果。
• bethekidyouwant认为作者在成功生成代码后无理由地称之为失败，且使用ChatGPT的免费版本是个大胆的选择。
• Radle认为如果提供完整的文档和示例程序，作者可能会得到更好的结果。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在编程任务中的实际能力和局限性，特别是它们是否能处理新颖或复杂的任务。
• 对不同模型的表现和使用方法有不同看法，部分评论者认为提供更多背景信息和工具可以提升LLM的表现。
• 部分评论者质疑文章所选模型的适用性和文章的高评价。
• 对LLM的机制和人类推理机制的类比和对比也是讨论的一个重要方面。

With the rise of LLM systems (or “AI” as they are annoyingly called), the term “
vibe coding
” is all the rage recently. Vibe coding is when you rely almost entirely on these “AI” system to write your code for you via a series of drawn-out conversations.
Putting on my cranky old man hat, I find most of it rather frustrating. Now I’m not some retro-sycophant who refuses to use modern tools. I’ve been a software professional for over 30 years at this point and I’ve used lots of tools throughout the years. Many that were cool and hip have long since disappeared or fallen out of fashion. I’ve also actually used these AI systems myself to help figure out some code. I find they function really well as a better search engine for documentation and can also serve as a way to “rubber duck” ideas and get some outlines. Any code I get back rarely seems to work as-is, but it often can provide ideas for something I hadn’t considered or perhaps point out something I did not know about.
After all, today’s technology is complex and it is not always easy to find what you need in the documentation.
But how does vibe coding work with something far simpler, such as the simplest programming language of them all: BASIC?
I suspect this might be a little tricker than it first appears. First of all, usage of BASIC largely predates the internet so there is far less BASIC code out there for LLMs to learn from. Many online retro BASIC books and docs are often scanned copies rather than easily digested plain text. Also, BASIC is not a single language, but more of an umbrella term for a family of languages all of which have the same “vibe”
1
, but often very different commands and capabilities, some of which rely heavily on PEEKs and POKEs to really take advantage of their system’s features
2
. And those ancient forms of API calls are poorly documented online.
So this should be an interesting challenge and to make it even slightly trickier, I’m going to use Atari BASIC rather than a much more common Microsoft BASIC variant, such as AppleSoft. Why? Because this is an Atari newsletter and I have plenty of Atari equipment to test things with. Alas, I don’t have any Apple II-era systems.
With that said, I will be using the
Atari800MacX emulator
because it makes it easy to paste in the generated code.
Now with all that out of the way, which LLM AI system should we try? Considering
ChatGPT
is the most commonly known and one most are familiar with, that’s I’m using for this experiment, although
Anthropic Claude
is also great for use with coding.
To do proper vibe coding, I need to refrain from correcting the generated code or even telling the AI what exactly is wrong.
Hello World
So what should be do first? Let’s start with a typical first BASIC program, the precursor to “Hello World”.
Prompt: Please write me a simple program in Atari BASIC that repeatedly prints “Hello, World” to the screen.
ChatGPT aced this simple test. I have to say, I do love seeing “GOTO 10” like that!
Draw a Circle
Atari BASIC does not have a built-in way to draw a circle so let’s ask for that:
Prompt: Write me an Atari BASIC program that draws a blue circle in graphics mode 7.
So far, the vibes are flowing. This program ran perfectly, although it only drew a rough, dotted circle.
I asked it for a solid outline instead of a dotted outline and it came back with this code:
10 GRAPHICS 7
20 COLOR 1
30 X=80:Y=48:R=30
40 A=0
50 X1=X+R*COS(A)
60 Y1=Y+R*SIN(A)
70 FOR A=0 TO 6.28 STEP .05
80 X2=X+R*COS(A)
90 Y2=Y+R*SIN(A)
100 DRAWTO X2,Y2
110 X1=X2:Y1=Y2
120 NEXT A
130 GOTO 130
That drew a solid outline using DRAWTO, but it did not set the starting position correctly.
It was able to fix things, however:

data.title: The Gentoo Perl versioning scheme
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary:
Gentoo的Perl版本方案解决了上游Perl版本与Gentoo版本不一致的问题。Perl上游使用两种版本方案，其中一种是浮点形式的"浮动"版本，这与Gentoo的版本排序不兼容。例如，Perl中1.1和1.10被视为相同版本，而Gentoo则按整数序列排序。

**解决方案**是将上游版本转换为一致的Gentoo版本，同时保留上游的排序顺序。对于包含多个"."或以"v"开头的版本，按整数序列处理。对于"浮动"版本，则通过补零和分组转换为"v-版本"形式。例如，1.1转换为1.100，再变为1.100.0。

通过使用`Gentoo::PerlMod::Version`工具，可以自动完成这种转换，确保在Perl版本比较中保持一致性。相比之下，其他规范化方案可能导致比较问题或版本冲突。

1.2

The Gentoo Perl Versioning Scheme
A common observation/confusion people have is that the versions used on Perl related things in Gentoo don't directly correspond to upstream versions.
This is because Upstream uses 2 different schemes, and one of those schemes is fundamentally incompatible with Gentoos.
The Problem
In most people's mind, this is how version numbers sort:
1.0
1.1
1.5
1.10
1.15
1.20
1.45
This is because you read
.
as a delimiter for multiple integers.
However, in Perl, those same versions sort as follows:
1.0
1.1  1.10
1.15
1.20
1.45
1.5
Because these versions are all treated as floating point, and yes,
1.1
and
1.10
are the
same
version.
perl -E 'say version->parse( q[1.1] ) <=> version->parse( q[1.10] )'
# 0
To make matters interesting, a leading
v
on a Perl version, or the presence of 2 or more
.
's imply a sort order closer to Gentoos. And so, the net result is this mess:
perl -E'say for sort map { version->parse($_) } qw(  1.0 1.10 1.1 1.10 1.15 1.20 1.45 v1.2 v1.3 v1.4 v1.1 v1.100 )'
# 1.0
# v1.1
# v1.2
# v1.3
# v1.4
# 1.10
# 1.1
# 1.10
# v1.100
# 1.15
# 1.20
# 1.45
Yes, if you realised
v1.100 == 1.1 == 1.10
but
v1.1 != 1.1
you were paying enough attention.
Confused? Good. So is everyone else who touches Perl versions, and the
whole host of related historical nightmares
Our Solution
The solution we employ is to decode upstreams version scheme and translate it into a consistent scheme that, after being translated, preserves upstreams sorting order when translated to gentoo versions, and we use this practically everywhere:
On Package Versions
In dependency specifications
This means as long as you're familiar with the translation process, you can get highly predictable results instead of a random fractal of confusion.
Gentoo::PerlMod::Version
(
dev-perl/Gentoo-PerlMod-Version
) is a reference implementation of this translation, and it can be used effectively blindly to translate upstream versions to downstream versions.
Install that package and run
gentoo-perlmod-version.pl SOME_CPAN_VERSION
to obtain the Gentoo version.
And we then hard-code the "real" upstream version inside the package (because its impossible to convert Gentoo versions generically to upstream ones, because you don't know which of the many formats it will take)
Conversion of v-Versions
Upstream does have some version schemes that we can use verbatim:
Any version with more than one
.
can be treated as an integer sequence like Gentoo Versions
Any version with a leading
v
can be treated an integer sequence like Gentoo Versions (after stripping the leading v)
Conversion of "Floating" versions
First, to understand how this works, you have to first understand how "v-Versions" are converted and compared with "Floating" version upstream:
Each digit group after the first is interpreted as 3 digits in the range 000-999
The values are concatenated to create the tail
So, for example, upstream:
1.1.2
means
1.001002
,
1.20.30
means
1.020030
, etc.
Our conversion to Gentoo versions basically applies the opposite of this, to convert a "Floating" version into a "v-Version" (without the "v")
Take the floating point number
Pad its tail to a multiple of 3 digits with trailing zeros
Split the tail into groups of 3 digits
Strip any leading
0
's from each group
Ensure there is a minimum of 3 groups of digits (with each at having at least one digit per group)
So for example:
1.1    ->   1.100 -> 1.100.0
1.001  ->   1.1.0
1.0001 ->   1.000100 -> 1.000.100 -> 1.0.100
And you can find a large table of other examples in the tests for
Gentoo::PerlMod::Version
The End Result
You can thus, pump Gentoo versions for Perl packages into Perl's version comparison, and it will still treat the normalized verions the same as the pre-normalized ones.
perl -MGentoo::PerlMod::Version=gentooize_version -E'say gentooize_version($_) for sort map { version->parse($_) } qw( 1.0 1.10 1.1 1.10 1.15 1.20 1.45 v1.2 v1.3 v1.4 v1.100 )'
# 1.0.0
# 1.2.0
# 1.3.0
# 1.4.0
# 1.100.0
# 1.100.0
# 1.100.0
# 1.100.0
# 1.150.0
# 1.200.0
# 1.450.0
perl -E'say q[GOOD] if version->parse(q[1.0001]) == version->parse(q[1.0.100]) ' # GOOD
Competing Normalisation Schemes
Some competing normalisations have issues in that they don't retain their comparison positions when fed back into Perl comparison functions, and are thus simply less desirable because it requires much more effort to reason about how they work.
They can also risk colliding with alternative existing forms upstream so the risk would occur that upstream could legally ship a new version such that a new version and an old version normalised to the same version gentoo side, and this is something we wish to avoid.

data.title: Super-resolution microscopes reveal new details of cells and disease
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种突破光学显微镜分辨率极限的“超分辨率显微技术”，使科学家能够更清晰地观察活细胞内的动态过程。传统光学显微镜由于光的衍射限制，无法分辨距离小于250纳米的物体，而电子显微镜虽有更高分辨率，但只能用于死细胞且图像为黑白。新的超分辨率技术，如单分子定位显微术、受激发射损耗显微术和结构光照显微术，通过使用荧光标记和特殊光学手段，能将分辨率提升至100纳米甚至10纳米以下，帮助科学家深入了解细胞运作机制及疾病成因，尤其在神经疾病、癌症和病毒感染研究中取得重要进展。

Powerful microscopes are affording new views of cellular processes. These include details of DNA replication in the nucleus of a mouse cell shown at left; the cell’s replication machinery appears green, already-replicated DNA is red and DNA bundled into chromatin is blue. At center, the cytoskeleton’s actin fibers in mouse connective tissue cells are seen in yellow; cellular DNA is stained blue. Shown at right is a human cell dividing in two; its genetic material is labeled in red, and the spindle apparatus that pulls the sister chromatids apart is labeled in green.
Technology
Super-resolution microscopes showcase the inner lives of cells
Advanced light microscopy techniques have come into their own — and are giving scientists a new understanding of human biology and what goes wrong in disease
By
Katarina Zimmer

Using a tiny, spherical glass lens sandwiched between two brass plates, the 17th century Dutch microscopist
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
was the first to officially describe red blood cells and sperm cells in human tissues, and observe
“animalcules” — bacteria and protists
— in the water of a lake.
Increasingly powerful light microscopes
followed, revealing cell organelles like the nucleus and energy-producing mitochondria. But by 1873, scientists realized there was a limit to the level of detail. When light passes through a lens, the light gets spread out through diffraction. This means that two objects can’t be distinguished if they’re less than roughly 250 nanometers (250 billionths of a meter) apart — instead, they’ll appear as a blur. That put the inner workings of cell structures off limits.
Electron microscopy, which uses electron beams instead of light, offers higher resolution. But the resulting black-and-white images make it hard tell proteins apart, and the method only works on dead cells.

Now, however, optics engineers and physicists have developed sophisticated tricks to overcome the diffraction limit of light microscopes, opening up a new world of detail. These
“super-resolution” light microscopy
techniques can distinguish objects down to 100 nanometers and sometimes even less than 10 nanometers. Scientists attach tiny, colored fluorescent tags to individual proteins or bits of DNA, often in living cells where they can watch them in action. As a result, they are now filling in key knowledge gaps about how cells work and what goes wrong in neurological diseases and cancers, or during viral infections.
“We can really see new biology — things that we were hoping to see but hadn’t seen before,” says molecular cell biologist
Lothar Schermelleh
, who directs an imaging center at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. Here’s some of what scientists are learning in this new age of light microscopy.
Overcoming the diffraction limit
Super-resolution microscopy uses a variety of techniques to detect detail that would normally be hidden by the diffraction limit, Schermelleh explains. Single-molecule localization microscopy, for instance, takes advantage of the fact that spots on an image are easier to localize with precision when they appear in isolation rather than clustered together. Scientists label the molecules of interest with fluorescent tags designed to spontaneously emit light. As the probes twinkle on and off, computational models estimate exactly where each molecule is located — and reconstruct a high-resolution image of the sample.
Another technique, stimulated emission depletion, scans the samples with lasers that are surrounded by a second, donut-shaped ring of lasers that cancel out the fluorescent light around the area of interest, sharpening the microscope’s resolution. A third method, called structured illumination microscopy, illuminates samples with a striped pattern of light. These stripes interfere with the light emanating from the sample in ways that allow scientists to infer additional detail about the image.

data.title: XSLT: A Precision Tool for the Future of Structured Transformation
data.author: protomolecool
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了XSLT（可扩展样式表转换语言）在企业级XML数据处理中的重要性和应用前景。尽管现代开发趋势偏向JSON和微服务，XSLT仍在金融、医疗、法律、教育和数字出版等需要高精度和结构化的领域中发挥关键作用。XSLT通过声明式模式匹配实现简洁高效的XML转换，具有模块化工作流、数据互操作性、金融数据交换、内容重用等优势。其核心功能包括流式处理、模板匹配、XPath支持、模块化重用、错误处理和处理非XML数据（如JSON）等。XSLT 3.0的演进使其能够应对现代数据挑战，尤其在构建可扩展、可维护的转换系统中具有重要价值。许多团队因不熟悉XSLT的声明式优势而转向繁琐的过程式代码，导致开发周期变慢、系统脆弱。XSLT在未来仍将是结构化转换的重要工具。

  ◦ **zabil**：认为XSLT帮助其深入理解了XPath，尽管现在不常用，但XPath仍然在使用。

  ◦ **DonHopkins**：认为XSLT标准委员会由不同编程范式的代表组成，导致标准复杂而不统一，实际工作中常需借助JavaScript解决XSLT问题。

争议焦点：
• **XSLT的实用性和复杂性**：部分开发者认为XSLT强大但过于复杂且难以维护，而另一些开发者则欣赏其声明式特性和历史应用。
• **XSLT生态系统的停滞**：开发者对XSLT工具和创新的缺乏表示不满，特别是与其他现代技术对比时。

总的来说，讨论围绕XSLT的历史应用、技术优缺点及其在现代技术环境中的适应性展开。

44633384.article_content:
XSLT: A Precision Tool for the Future of Structured Transformation July 19, 2025 Vasu Chakkera Vasu Chakkera gives a summary of some of the varied enterprise uses for XSLT Introduction While modern development trends lean toward JSON and microservices, XML continues to operate quietly but powerfully beneath the surface in enterprise domains like finance, healthcare, legal, education, and digital publishing. In these spaces, where precision, structure, and longevity are non-negotiable, XSLT (Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations) remains one of the most capable — and often underappreciated — tools in the transformation toolkit. And yet, many teams make the costly mistake of sidelining XSLT in favor of verbose procedural code written by general-purpose developers unfamiliar with its declarative strengths. The result? Slower development cycles, brittle pipelines, and underperforming systems. This article explores why XSLT continues to be essential , how it enables scalable, maintainable XML transformations, and how its evolution — particularly in version 3.0 — has equipped it for modern data challenges. Why XSLT Still Matters XSLT was purpose-built to transform structured XML. Unlike procedural code, it operates through declarative pattern-matching, allowing transformations to be expressed succinctly and cleanly. It excels in: Modular publishing workflows (DITA, DocBook, JATS) Data interoperability in healthcare (HL7, CDA) Financial data exchange (MISMO, FpML, XBRL) Assessment and testing systems (QTI transformations) Content reuse and restructuring in media and legal publishing Canonical data modeling for data lakes and ETL pipelines Its predictable, rule-based execution model reduces maintenance effort and makes it easier to onboard new developers into a project — when written well. Core Capabilities of XSLT (Modern and Classic) Whether you're using XSLT 1.0 in a legacy system or taking advantage of XSLT 2.0/3.0 in modern environments, the language offers deep transformation power. Below are some of its most valuable features — many of which are enhanced in XSLT 3.0 but rooted in the strengths of the language as a whole. 1. Streaming: Efficient Memory Use on Large Documents Modern XSLT processors (such as Saxon) support streaming, enabling processing of large XML documents without loading them entirely into memory. Use case: HL7 records, QTI test banks, financial batch data. Streaming ensures scalability and performance even with very large input documents. 2. Template Matching and Declarative Control Flow At its heart, XSLT uses pattern matching instead of step-by-step loops. This model is more maintainable for tree-based transformations.

This eliminates complex traversal logic found in procedural alternatives and allows for clean rule-based transformations. 3. XPath: The Power Behind the Simplicity XSLT leverages XPath for selecting and navigating XML content. Over the years, XPath has evolved to support sequences, functions, and type-aware expressions, enabling sophisticated queries with minimal syntax. In XSLT 2.0 and above, XPath also supports regular expressions, date math, grouping, and more. 4. Modularization and Reuse XSLT encourages reuse through: Named templates and modes Import/include mechanisms Function libraries (especially in XSLT 2.0+) Packages (XSLT 3.0) This enables teams to build transformation libraries that scale and evolve. 5. Error Handling and Robust Pipelines While early versions of XSLT lacked error management, XSLT 3.0 introduced xsl:try/xsl:catch, allowing graceful error handling in production pipelines. This feature enables resilience in systems where unpredictable inputs are common. 6. Working with Non-XML Data: JSON, Maps, and Arrays Modern XSLT allows developers to ingest JSON and work with key-value or array-based structures, thanks to features introduced in version 3.0. JSON round-trip example: This bridges the XML world with modern REST APIs and web front ends. 7. Schema-Awareness for Validation and Typed Processing Schema-aware XSLT allows input and output documents to be validated against XSDs. This is crucial in highly regulated domains (e.g., healthcare, legal, finance).

  ◦ **password4321**：提到XSLT在讨论中被重新关注，并提及其他技术如SXML/SSAX。
  ◦ **Devasta**：认为放弃XML是Web发展的错误，XML相关的功能如客户端模板、验证、数据绑定等非常有用。

补充讨论：
• **XSLT与其他技术的对比**：
  ◦ **DonHopkins**：认为XSLT标准委员会由不同编程范式的代表组成，导致标准复杂而不统一，实际工作中常需借助JavaScript解决XSLT问题。

争议焦点：
• **XSLT的实用性和复杂性**：部分开发者认为XSLT强大但过于复杂且难以维护，而另一些开发者则欣赏其声明式特性和历史应用。
• **XSLT生态系统的停滞**：开发者对XSLT工具和创新的缺乏表示不满，特别是与其他现代技术对比时。

总的来说，讨论围绕XSLT的历史应用、技术优缺点及其在现代技术环境中的适应性展开。

data.title: AI is killing the web – can anything save it?
data.author: edward
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AI，尤其是ChatGPT及其竞争对手的崛起，如何对互联网的经济模式构成威胁。Cloudflare的首席执行官Matthew Prince提到，大型媒体公司正担忧AI对网络安全的威胁。文章探讨了AI对网络的破坏性影响，以及是否有可能拯救互联网。此外，文章还简要介绍了其他商业新闻，包括Nvidia说服政府投资“自主”AI的努力、特朗普铜关税的后果、美国对稀土矿的大笔投资、Kraft Heinz等食品巨头的困境以及酒店品牌在印度的发展潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与搜索引擎的变化对网络社区和内容质量的影响

不同观点：
• dehrmann认为，Stack Overflow的访客减少是因为社区对重复、研究不充分或作业类问题的排斥，导致用户将问题转向其他地方。这表明社区规则的严格可能驱散了部分用户。
• sameerds对AI取代臃肿的、充满广告的网络持乐观态度，认为这可能让网络回归到更个人化和去中心化的时代，如Usenet和IRC。这反映了一种对早期互联网时代的怀旧情绪。
• inopinatus用比喻的方式指出，2022年后的内容可能因AI的介入而变得“有毒”或不可靠，暗示AI生成内容对信息质量的潜在影响。
• nonvibecoding认为，网络社区的独特性和灵魂早在AI普及之前就已经开始消逝，AI只是让这个问题更加明显。这强调了网络同质化的问题。
• Roark66指责谷歌搜索质量的下降是导致人们转向AI的原因，并认为AI可能通过筛选出优质链接来复兴网络。这表明搜索引擎的衰落而非AI是主要问题。
• snickerbockers对网络的现状持批评态度，认为它已经偏离了超文本的初衷，并被搜索引擎和动态内容所主导。这反映了对技术复杂性和商业化的不满。
• ddmichael强调高质量内容和人类撰写的新闻的重要性，暗示AI生成内容可能无法替代人类创作。
• benjaminclauss对SEO被AI工具挑战感到兴奋，认为这可能改变传统搜索引擎优化 landscape，减少不必要的内容。
• poulpy123将AI视为压垮网络的最后一根稻草，认为SEO和谷歌的放任自流早已使网络质量下降。
• hollerith对浏览器作为访问互联网信息的工具感到不满，认为LLM服务可以减少对浏览器的依赖，从而提高信息获取效率。
• alganet主张减少协作和竞争，提倡个人观点的独立性，认为这可能改善网络和更广泛的社会问题。
• franze质疑网络是否值得拯救，特别提到了社交媒体、假新闻和回声室效应的问题，暗示网络可能已经病入膏肓。
• jlarocco认为广告而非AI是导致网络变糟的主要原因，并指出这个问题已经存在了20年。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于网络质量下降的原因，一些人认为是搜索引擎和广告的问题，另一些人则归咎于AI和SEO。
• 怀旧情绪和对早期互联网特性的向往在多个评论中体现，尤其是对个人博客、社区网站和去中心化平台的怀念。
• 对AI的看法存在分歧，有人认为AI可能复兴网络，有人则认为AI会进一步破坏网络生态。
• 讨论中多次提到信息质量和获取的效率问题，反映了对当前网络环境的不满和对改进的期望。

data.title: We benchmarked Cyberpunk 2077 on Mac M1 to M4 – the numbers don't lie
data.author: high_na_euv
data.article_summary: 《Cyberpunk 2077》现在可以在Mac上原生运行，尤其是借助Apple的MetalFX升频技术，游戏表现良好。Tom's Guide的测试团队对多款现代Mac进行了基准测试，包括从2021年的M1 Max MacBook Pro到最新的M4 Max Mac Studio。结果显示，尽管Mac的游戏性能仍无法与顶级游戏PC相比，但通过调整设置并启用MetalFX分辨率缩放，可以获得不错的帧率。要运行游戏，Mac需配备M1及以上芯片和至少16GB内存。只有M3及以上芯片支持光线追踪。总体来看，游戏在Mac上的表现相当不错，但需要适当优化设置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Mac上运行《赛博朋克2077》的图形设置、性能表现以及Mac硬件的适宜性。

不同观点：
• **al_borland**：认为Mac上的模糊预设图形设置（"For Your Mac"）被视为不好的事情是不公平的。他指出，大多数人只想玩游戏，而不是花费大量时间调整设置。他以Nintendo Switch的成功为例，说明普通玩家并不优先考虑图形和帧率，而是游戏体验本身。

• **nottorp**：强调了Mac版本的一个优势，即在GoG或Steam上购买游戏时，Mac版本是与Windows版本捆绑销售的，无需在App Store上再次付费。

• **jug**：表达了对Mac硬件散热问题的担忧，特别是在玩游戏时风扇在接近100°C时才会明显启动。虽然有人告诉他Mac可以承受这样的高温，但他仍然表示怀疑。

• **zeld4**：分享了自己的实际体验，使用M1 Pro的Mac运行《赛博朋克2077》已经相当流畅，并希望更多游戏能够在发布时支持Mac，提供更好的兼容性。

• **high_na_euv**：指出即使Mac硬件配置较高，如Mac Studio M3 Ultra，可能也无法与同等价位的Windows游戏PC在运行《赛博朋克2077》时相媲美，暗示Windows PC在游戏性能上的优势。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Mac上的图形设置和性能表现是否被不公平地视为不好的事情。al_borland认为普通玩家不优先考虑这些，而high_na_euv则强调Windows PC在游戏性能上的优势。
• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：nottorp提到的捆绑销售模式为Mac用户提供了便利；jug对Mac硬件散热问题的担忧反映了部分用户对Mac长时间高负载下稳定性的疑虑。zeld4的实际体验为Mac用户提供了正面参考，强调了Mac在游戏兼容性上的潜力。

Nearly five years after launch,
Cyberpunk 2077 now runs natively on Macs
— and it runs well, if you rely on Apple's MetalFX upscaling tech.
I know because here at Tom's Guide our crack team of testing experts has been hard at work in our lab this week benchmarking how well the game runs on a slew of modern Macs.
Now we have numbers for how well Cyberpunk 2077 runs on everything from a 2021 M1 Max MacBook Pro to a cutting-edge M4 Max Mac Studio, and the results should get you excited if you've been dreaming of playing CD Projekt Red's cyberpunk RPG.

Because our testing reveals that while even the latest Macs can't match the gaming prowess of the
best gaming PCs
, if you fine-tune the settings and enable MetalFX resolution scaling you can get some pretty good framerates playing
Cyberpunk 2077
on your Mac.
Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Mac system requirements
(Image credit: Future)
Before we dig into the data, I wanted to quickly remind you that Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate runs on
most
Macs with Apple silicon—but there are some key caveats you should know about.
Notably, to run it your Mac must be packing an M1 chip or newer and have at least 16GB of unified memory. So we couldn't test how well it runs on an entry-level
MacBook Air M1
or
MacBook Air M2,
for example, because they only have 8GB of memory.
On top of that, only Macs with M3 or newer chips support the game's ray tracing features. So as you're looking through our test results, remember that only the M3 and M4 Macs can even run the game with ray tracing enabled.

Thursday (July 17), and our testing team immediately downloaded a few copies and started benchmarking it on every Mac we could lay our hands on.
So while we haven't yet had a chance to comprehensively benchmark it on every possible Mac configuration, we do have a nice spread of test results that gives you a good sense of how well the game runs on Apple silicon old and new.
The quick answer is: pretty well! However, you have to give yourself over to Apple's MetalFX resolution scaling and the nebulous "For Your Mac" graphical preset in order to get a decent framerate playing Cyberpunk 2077 on most Macs.
When we did our best to fine-tune the graphical settings to match what we use when running Cyberpunk 2077 benchmarks on Windows PCs, the framerate tanked. If you'd like to get a sense of how different these two configurations look, click to zoom in on the screenshots below.

On the oldest Macs that did not support ray tracing, we used the "Ultra" preset instead.

data.title: Linux Distros for Gaming: CachyOS Takes Over, According to ProtonDB
data.author: ekianjo
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论2025年夏季Linux游戏发行版的最新变化。CachyOS取代Ubuntu，成为增长最快的发行版，Ubuntu的游戏用户份额从2019年的40%降至不到8%。CachyOS不仅在游戏领域增长迅速，还在DistroWatch排名中位居榜首。Fedora和Linux Mint分别保持约10%和12%的份额，而Manjaro和Pop!_OS则大幅下滑，Manjaro即将跌出榜单，Pop!_OS因多年未更新也失去用户信任。Nobara和Bazzite保持稳定，但增长停滞，未来可能受到SteamOS扩展的挑战。文章提醒，数据来自ProtonDB，可能存在偏差，不能完全代表所有Linux用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Arch衍生版操作系统的适用性及对用户技术能力的要求

不同观点：
• [支持观点] [scheeseman486] 认为Arch衍生版（如Garuda Linux）是一个不错的选择，特别是对想要简化操作的Arch用户。他以自己从EndeavourOS迁移过来的经验为例，认为这种系统非常适合用来玩游戏，提供了简化的Arch体验，适合那些不想处理复杂安装过程的人。

• [反对观点] [constantcrying] 强烈反对推广Arch衍生版，认为这些版本是“猴子爪子”（比喻带来诅咒的愿望），尤其是对技术能力不足的用户。他指出，如果一个人无法安装Arch Linux，那么他也不具备处理Arch系统维护的能力。当问题出现时，这些用户会感到困惑和失望，因为他们缺乏自我解决问题的能力。此外，他认为像Manjaro这样的Arch衍生版往往带来更多问题，将它们推荐给技术能力不足的用户只会带来失望和挫败感，进而损害Linux桌面和Linux游戏的声誉。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点] 争议的核心在于Arch衍生版是否适合技术能力较低的用户。一方认为这些版本简化了Arch的使用，适合新手或只想专注于游戏的用户；另一方则认为，技术能力不足的用户使用Arch衍生版最终会带来更多的问题和负面体验，可能损害整个Linux社区的声誉。

• [论据对比] 支持者以个人使用经验为例，强调这些系统简化了Arch的复杂性，对特定用户群体有帮助。反对者则从用户技术能力的角度出发，强调缺乏技术背景的用户在使用这些系统时会面临的潜在问题和风险。

• [对社区影响的讨论] 反对者进一步提出，推广不适合用户的操作系统可能会对Linux桌面和游戏社区带来负面影响，这体现了对社区整体健康发展的关注。

44633758.article_content:
It’s summer. Usually everything is pretty quiet. There’s no reason to make waves unless you are on the beach. Just out of curiosity, I was checking a few days ago what happens to the Linux distros used for gaming, expecting no change at all from a few months ago. Boy, I was wrong. I told you last time that
CachyOS was the fastest growing distro
back in May 2025. You would expect such statements to tamper down over time: you can’t usually grow forever on a very competitive market. Well… until now.
First before the results, the usual disclaimer, as this data comes from
ProtonDB
:
This may not be representative of all types of Linux users. I’m sure this is not what your AWS engineer uses on EC2.
This may not be completely representative of all Linux gamers either. But I’d wage this is actually a good predictor where the market is going to shift. We saw first that
Manjaro
was getting the boot here first, before going under pretty much everywhere.
There may be some additional biases, due to whoever used ProtonDB.
Flatpak
is NOT a distro, but that’s what Steam reports when it’s running on Flatpak, and Flatpak being distro independent we report it as a separate environment, if that makes sense. Feel free to ignore it if you wish.
Arch Linux
is
Arch Linux on desktop
. The Steam Deck’s OS is reported as
HoloISO
, not
Arch Linux
, so stop trying to claim that Arch is first because of the Steam Deck! This is mainly data reported from desktop PCs, so no,
SteamOS
is not a thing at the moment on such machines. This may change as Valve starts providing official support beyond the
Steam Deck
.
Now on to the results. You might want to click on the picture to enlarge it.
Now let’s review the changes in more details.
CachyOS overtakes Ubuntu
It seems almost unreal.
Ubuntu
is now becoming a minority choice for gamers on Linux. Back in 2019, it was almost the default with more than 40% of gamers using
Ubuntu
. Now, look how far things have gone:
Ubuntu
is at less than 8% usage share! And
CachyOS
, continuing on its steady growth, has overtaken
Ubuntu
as it reached 8.3% based on the last figures. Even you were to discount
CachyOS
,
Ubuntu
would be on the third spot for several months now after
Fedora
anyway. Canonical is clearly losing steam, and very fast, at least for those who care about games.
Note that CachyOS is not just a popular topic for gamers, it turns out that it’s reached the top spot on the
DistroWatch ranking
too, by far. So it’s getting noticed. If you are interested to know more about their features and options for customization, you can also check their
wiki
. There are also recent comparisons of the performance of
Bazzite
,
SteamOS
and
CachyOS
on the Steam Deck, such as in
this video
(get ready for some rough French accent!) and while
CachyOS
performs well overall, it does not seem to bring any advantage compared to
SteamOS
in terms of FPS in games. At least for this device.
Back to the top of the ranking,
Fedora
seems to solidify around 10% more or less, and
Mint
is just a step beyond that with typically about 12%, making it stay at a solid 2nd place as well behind
Arch
that remains the undefeated master for many years now. As
CachyOS
grows, it may start to cannibalize some of the share of
Arch Linux
, but so far it looks like its growth has been mostly out of non-Arch Linux users.
Losing Big: Pop!_OS and Manjaro
Manjaro
is landing into the depths of the ranking, now below 3% - it won’t be too long until its name is removed from the list. Nothing surprising if you have been following the
drama around the distro
, and the fact that it completely lacks a reason for existing in 2025 compared to what’s already out there.
Pop!_OS
also barely makes it above 3% - no wonder since it’s not been updated for years, and the
System76
team seems to be more focused on
COSMIC
than anything else these days. Too bad, because at its height,
Pop!_OS
was a great
Ubuntu
alternative, with a lot of useful features baked in and a very stable experience. It could have been the new
Mint
it they had managed to keep resources allocated to work on it. Now, it’s not clear that they would be able to claw back some share even if they magically released a new version tomorrow: I’d say the trust is gone after so little activity for such a long time. In a way,
Mint
is the excellent counter example. It does not make waves, barely anyone talks about it, but sticks to a high quality distro release schedule, and the results speak for themselves: stability and trust is paramount.
Holding up: Bazzite, Nobara and NixOS
Despite the changes around them, both
Nobara
and
Bazzite
seem to keep hanging on at a stable share, close to 5% each. However it seems that both have stopped growing at that point and may be stuck at the current threshold. I’m not sure there is however much future when it comes to
Bazzite
, since
SteamOS
will eventually be rolling out to more and more devices out there. I guess it depends how much Valve does in terms of hardware support

data.title: Diary of a Startup – the rise and fall of ArsDigita
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《创业日记：ArsDigita的兴衰》讲述了一家从创立之初就盈利的科技公司，如何因风险投资的介入而走向衰败。ArsDigita由Eve Andersson和同伴们在1998年成立，初期凭借实用产品、尊重程序员和免费提供软件及培训赢得了市场。然而，随着风险资本的进入，公司文化从慈善转为贪婪，技术和管理上的无能导致公司倒闭，4000多万美元的风投资金被浪费殆尽。文章强调了保持技术初心和管理能力对企业成功的重要性，并通过ArsDigita社区系统（ACS）的开发与开源，展示了如何有效解决重复性技术问题。最终，公司的失败为软件产品开发和企业管理提供了深刻教训。

Diary of a Start-Up
the rise and fall of ArsDigita
and lessons from the world of venture capital
by
Eve Andersson
This is a story about a company.  A company that was profitable from Day 1.
A company that built products that were useful to many other companies.  A
company that had ethics, that treated the breadwinners (programmers) with
respect, a company that could afford to help people and give away software
and training, while still having enough left over to grow and save a few
$million in the bank.
That is, until the venture capitalists arrived on the scene.  Lying to
customers and employees became commonplace.  Greed replaced philanthropy
as each of
the company's unique programs was dropped.  But, this is
a company, and the goal is to make money -- any positive impact on the
world is secondary, right?  The real question is: how much money did they
make?
The technical and managerial incompetence of the VCs and those they hired
drove the company into the ground.  All but 10 of the 240 employees were
fired, laid off, or quit.  All of the $40+ million in venture capital was
squandered.  The monthly operating profit turned to loss as more talentless
executives were hired who threw out the company's old, useful products and put their blind
faith in engineers who spent millions building complicated software that
solved no business problems.
This is a story that will teach you something about building a software product,
about profitably running a company, and about what can happen if unqualified
organizations obtain control.
The Birth of ArsDigita
Since the early days of the Web, I had been building web sites for
big-name clients in California with my friend Aurelius Prochazka.
Meanwhile, Philip Greenspun and two of his friends,
Jin Choi and Tracy Adams, were doing similar work out in Massachusetts.
When I moved to Massachusetts in 1998, we joined forces and were quickly
able to quickly attract high profile clients, such as Levi Strauss, Environmental Defense,
and MIT Press.
Our band of programmers, called ArsDigita ("Digital Arts"), was profitable
from the beginning.  We had no office, no marketing staff, no letterhead.
But we did have a few thousand dollars' worth of computer equipment
and our five motivated selves.
The Birth of the ACS
It didn't take long for us to realize that we were solving some of
the same problems over and over again for each of our sites.  It doesn't
matter if a site sells custom-made slacks, lets people share their
photography knowledge with other enthusiasts,
helps people fight environmental battles against companies
polluting their groundwater,
facilitates the trading of financial instruments,
or helps people find the best combination of red, white, and sparkling
wines for their next soirée.
Every site we built needed:
to talk to a relational database management system (RDBMS) to facilitate
the collection of content from its users
a means for registering users and recognizing them upon their return
to the site
a permission system to enable administration of the entire site,
a section of the site, or an individual content item
a mechanism for grouping users so that they can be served content or
given permissions appropriately
Instead of reproducing this for each client, we wrote a general data model,
a few web pages, and some shared procedures, and called this collection
of code the ArsDigita Community System (ACS).
We distributed the ACS free and open-source, not merely to be altruistic,
but because it made sound business sense.  If you are doing professional
services, the best way to get your name out, have more clients find you
(yes, free marketing), and improve the code base is to share it with the
open-source world.
The ACS began as a small core of functionality, but more opportunities
for code reuse quickly arose.  Many of our clients wanted discussion
forums.  Quite a few needed ecommerce.  Polls and portals and intranets
and calendars and address books were repeatedly requested.  It would
have been foolish to build this functionality one-off for each client.
It would have been a wasted opportunity to build this only for ourselves
and not let our work reap the benefits of an open-source release.  Hence
we began the release of ACS modules that could run on top of the core.
Dozens of useful modules were created, and that is what led to the
adoption of the ACS by programmers and companies world-wide.

data.title: How to run an Arduino for years on a battery (2021)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何通过优化硬件和软件，使Arduino系统能够依靠电池运行数年。通常Arduino通过USB供电，但在自主项目中，如无线运动检测器，需使用电池供电。直接使用Arduino Uno R3板耗电较快，因此需自制Arduino系统并优化软件以节省功耗。

硬件方面，需使用ATMega328微控制器、电容、电阻、LED、晶振等元件，并通过电池直接供电以避免电压调节器耗电。软件方面，使用Arduino IDE编程，并通过JeeLib库将微控制器设置为睡眠模式以减少功耗。

具体步骤包括搭建电路、编写基础程序（如"blink"示例）并测试，最终通过JeeLib库进一步优化功耗，使系统在非工作状态下几乎不耗电。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于微控制器项目中低功耗模式、库文件的使用以及技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• [_ache_] 认为代码中的库文件包含有明显的错误，特别是 `#include <JeeLib.h;>` 这一句，并对该库的文档和项目本身的可靠性提出质疑，尤其是对项目网站可能被废弃或劫持表示担忧。
• [icedrop] 提到了图片加载问题，表明在查看相关内容时遇到技术故障，可能与页面资源或浏览器有关。
• [whatever1] 提出是否存在专门用于高效休眠和唤醒其他微控制器的微控制器，暗示某些微控制器可能在低功耗管理方面具有特殊功能。
• [xmprt] 认为在实际复杂项目中，尤其是在需要结合WiFi通信、传感器唤醒以及多线程并行运行的情况下，简单地使用低功耗模式并不实际，管理起来更加困难。

补充讨论：
• [ggm] 补充了关于RF（如WiFi或蓝牙）对电池消耗的影响，并提到通过固定点采样捕获和时钟协调来处理功耗问题。他还引用了历史上的技术例子，如GSM时代的Morse代码脉冲、Zigbee和6lowpan等在低功耗通信方面的应用。同时，提到通过LED闪烁代码远程读取信息的可能性，并引用了Newton设备和会议翻译耳机作为实际案例。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于低功耗模式在复杂项目中的实际可行性，特别是在需要结合多种通信方式和多线程操作的情况下，如何有效管理功耗和项目复杂性。
• 另外，关于JeeLib库的可靠性和文档不完善的问题也是讨论中的一个争议点。

总结：
讨论围绕微控制器项目中的低功耗实现展开，涉及到具体的技术细节如库文件使用、WiFi通信、多线程管理和具体技术实现案例。各方对低功耗模式的实际应用效果和复杂项目中的管理难度存在不同看法。同时，对具体库文件和文档的质量也提出了质疑。

How to Run an Arduino for Years on a Battery
June 17, 2021
â¢
15 min read
If you found this article after doing a search on Google, welcome! On this website you will find plenty of content around DIY home automation using open-source hardware. Enjoy the article!
For most of the Arduino tutorials you will find on this website, power is usually not an issue as the Arduino is powered by the USB cable coming from the computer. However, sometimes you want to build systems that are going to be autonomous and powered by a battery.
For example, you want to power a wireless motion detector just by using a set of batteries. The first idea would be to connect directly an Arduino board like the Arduino Uno R3 to a battery. Easy, right ? Well, it would work, but your battery would be depleted in a matter of days because some components like voltage regulators are always sucking power. So we need something better.
The first thing we need is to build our own Arduino system with just the minimal set of components. The second part is to optimise the software so that the system only consumes power when it is actually doing something. And thatâs exactly what we will see in this article.
Hardware & Software Requirements
You need several components to build you own Arduino system. The main piece of this project is of course the microcontroller that will run your Arduino sketches, like the
ATMega328
. You will need a chip with the Arduino bootloader. Buy your chip with it, it will make your life easier.
In a previous project I used a
FTDI breakout board
to program the Arduino chip directly on the breadboard. But for this project I wonât have any external power running on the breadboard so I will just use an Arduino Uno board to program the microcontroller.
To power the Arduino, you will need a battery. The best is to power the Arduino directly from the battery, so you donât have to use any voltage regulators that will suck some power. I used a
set of two AA batteries
(1.5V each) with a
battery holder
thus powering the microcontroller with around 3V, which is fine according to the
ATmega328 documentation
.
You will also need several components around the chip. You will need
one 10uF capacitor
,
two 22pF capacitors
,
one 10K Ohm resistor
,
one 220 Ohm resistor
,

Atmel ATmega328

Two 22pF capacitors

2 AA batteries
Breadboard and some jumper wires
On the software side, you just need the usual Arduino IDE. Note that in this tutorial, we will only cover a tiny part of the possibilities offered by the Arduino platform.
Hardware Configuration
This project is a bit complex to build, so be sure to follow the instructions. This is how it should look like at the end:
First, put the microcontroller in the center of the breadboard. You can then take care about the power: connect power lines on each side, connect the negative power rail to the two GND pins of the microcontroller, and the positive power rail to VCC, AVCC, and AREF. Also, add the 10uF capacitor between two power rails. Finally, add the battery to the system.
You also have to add the crystal between the X1 and X2 pins, with 22pF capacitors going from each pin to the ground. Also, you need to connect the RST pin to the positive power rail using a 10K Ohm resistor. To see if the system is working, connect the green LED in series with a 220 Ohm resistor to the digital pin 13 of the Arduino board, the other side going to the ground.

So now, we have an autonomous Arduino system. But it still consuming way too much power. Indeed, even when the LED is off, the Arduino chip is still active and consumes power. data.title: The current hype around autonomous agents, and what actually works in production
data.author: Dachande663
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了当前对2025年AI代理（AI agents）的过度 hype，并基于作者过去一年构建十几个生产级代理系统的经验，提出了三个关键现实问题：

1. **错误累积**：在多步骤工作流中，每步95%的可靠性在20步后成功率仅为36%，而生产系统需要99.9%以上的可靠性。当前技术下，自主多步骤工作流在数学上是不可能的。
   
2. **成本问题**：长对话导致token成本呈二次方增长，使得对话型代理在经济上不可行。成功的代理系统通常是无状态、专注于解决特定问题，而非持续对话。

3. **工具设计挑战**：构建生产级代理工具需要特别的工程设计，重点在于提供有效反馈和避免过度占用上下文窗口。

作者认为，当前对AI代理的预期过于乐观，实际成功的系统依赖于离散操作、验证步骤和人工干预点，而非完全自主的多步骤流程。
