44623207.article_content:
Everyone says 2025 is the year of AI agents. The headlines are everywhere: "Autonomous AI will transform work," "Agents are the next frontier," "The future is agentic." Meanwhile, I've spent the last year building many different agent systems that actually work in production. And that's exactly why I'm betting against the current hype.
I'm not some AI skeptic writing from the sidelines. Over the past year, I've built more than a dozen production agent systems across the entire software development lifecycle:
Development agents
: UI generators that create functional React components from natural language, code refactoring agents that modernize legacy codebases, documentation generators that maintain API docs automatically, and function generators that convert specifications into working implementations.
Data & Infrastructure agents
: Database operation agents that handle complex queries and migrations, DevOps automation AI systems managing infrastructure-as-code across multiple cloud providers.
Quality & Process agents
: AI-powered CI/CD pipelines that fix lint issues, generate comprehensive test suites, perform automated code reviews, and create detailed pull requests with proper descriptions.
These systems work. They ship real value. They save hours of manual work every day. And that's precisely why I think much of what you're hearing about 2025 being "the year of agents" misses key realities.
TL;DR: Three Hard Truths About AI Agents
After building 12+ production systems, here's what I've learned:
Error rates compound exponentially in multi-step workflows. 95% reliability per step = 36% success over 20 steps. Production needs 99.9%+.
Context windows create quadratic token costs. Long conversations become prohibitively expensive at scale.
The real challenge isn't AI capabilities, it's designing tools and feedback systems that agents can actually use effectively.
The Mathematical Reality No One Talks About
Here's the uncomfortable truth that every AI agent company is dancing around: error compounding makes autonomous multi-step workflows mathematically impossible at production scale.
Error Compounding in AI Agent Workflows
Let's do the math. If each step in an agent workflow has 95% reliability, which is optimistic for current LLMs,then:
5 steps = 77% success rate
10 steps = 59% success rate
20 steps = 36% success rate
Production systems need 99.9%+ reliability. Even if you magically achieve 99% per-step reliability (which no one has), you still only get 82% success over 20 steps. This isn't a prompt engineering problem. This isn't a model capability problem. This is mathematical reality.
My DevOps agent works precisely because it's not actually a 20-step autonomous workflow. It's 3-5 discrete, independently verifiable operations with explicit rollback points and human confirmation gates. The "agent" handles the complexity of generating infrastructure code, but the system is architected around the mathematical constraints of reliability.
Every successful agent system I've built follows the same pattern: bounded contexts, verifiable operations, and human decision points (sometimes) at critical junctions. The moment you try to chain more than a handful of operations autonomously, the math kills you.
The Token Economics That Don't Add Up
There's another mathematical reality that agent evangelists conveniently ignore: context windows create quadratic cost scaling that makes conversational agents economically impossible.
Here's what actually happens when you build a "conversational" agent:
Each new interaction requires processing ALL previous context
Token costs scale quadratically with conversation length
A 100-turn conversation costs $50-100 in tokens alone
Multiply by thousands of users and you're looking at unsustainable economics
I learned this the hard way when prototyping a conversational database agent. The first few interactions were cheap. By the 50th query in a session, each response was costing multiple dollars - more than the value it provided. The economics simply don't work for most scenarios.
Token Cost Scaling in Conversational Agents
My function generation agent succeeds because it's completely stateless: description → function → done. No context to maintain, no conversation to track, no quadratic cost explosion. It's not a "chat with your code" experience, it's a focused tool that solves a specific problem efficiently.
The most successful "agents" in production aren't conversational at all. They're smart, bounded tools that do one thing well and get out of the way.
The Tool Engineering Reality Wall
Even if you solve the math problems, you hit a different kind of wall: building production-grade tools for agents is an entirely different engineering discipline that most teams underestimate.
Tool calls themselves are actually quite precise now. The real challenge is tool design. Every tool needs to be carefully crafted to provide the right feedback without overwhelming the context window. You need

Columnists
32
Selling your digital soul to use Bluesky's DMs isn't just a bad idea, it's the law
32
Getting carded is one thing. A full strip search? Welcome to Britain
Rupert Goodwins
Mon 21 Jul 2025
//
09:02 UTC
Opinion
On June 10, social network Bluesky announced that in 15 days it would
introduce age verification
for UK users, to comply with the UK Online Safety Act. As this law threatens non-compliant content companies with eight-figure fines from July 25, you can see why. The how, however, is breathtakingly inexcusable.
Won't somebody think of the European children? Meta and Google put up their hands to help on the same day
READ MORE
As with many very bad ideas, it comes from a simple statement that discourages discussion: children are seeing damaging content online, from which they should be protected. If you choose not to be age-verified on UK Bluesky, you will not be able to view adult content nor use direct messaging. If you consent to age verification, you can. Sounds reasonable. Arguing about it implies selfishness at best, to say nothing of the worst.
Not so. Here goes.
There are only two things wrong with using age verification to shield kids from inappropriate content – the age verification bit and the inappropriate content bit. UK law and Bluesky's way of complying demonstrate both.
Starting with inappropriate content, of course, it has never in the history of the free world been effectively defined. It's case-by-case, currently including content about alcohol and gambling alongside explicit sexual material. Then there's non-sexual nudity, suggestive material, and, depending on who you talk to, discussions about gender and sexuality.
The list can be as broad as you like. Bluesky's own adult content filter settings allow a curiously granular set of fine-tuning switches including "potentially disturbing media." One presumes this switch just disconnects the internet.
You might not mind not being able to share a picture of that great new craft beer, or link to that fascinating question to which the answer is 93*. But many professional communities online, from medics to medievalists, will affirm how important it is to be able to talk to all sorts of people about all of humanity, including those that make your mythical maiden aunt blush. Moreover, social media is their glue. One of the great benefits of online life is bringing birds of a feather together, and environments that restrict how they flock are not conducive.
You can be sure that restrictions will tighten. Whatever algorithm is in place to identify inappropriate content, it'll be set as strictly as possible. Big fines if you're too lax. Nothing for over-zealousness. There's no moderating feedback path.
Even so, that may seem acceptable collateral damage if children can't see that stuff alongside the damaging material. Real life has age verification on lots of things, some more effective than others, but most worth keeping around. Why should online age verification be any different? Why not just verify and be done? Over to you, Bluesky.
The path Bluesky has chosen is Kids Web Services (KWS), a system controlled by Epic Games. Yes,
that Epic Games
. To verify yourself as an adult to Bluesky UK, you'll have to register with KWS. You don't have to use KWS if you're a kid – only if you're an adult, or "parent" as KWS will refer to you.
Stopping the rot when good software goes bad means new rules from the start

data.title: NIH limits scientists to six applications per year
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NIH对申请数量设置上限的政策及其引发的广泛讨论

不同观点：
• 支持设置申请上限：一些评论（如[randomizedalgs]）认为设置提交上限可以减少垃圾申请，让研究人员有更多时间专注于实际研究，而不是无休止地撰写基金申请。该观点提到CS项目已有类似规则，效果 positive。

• 反对设置申请上限，认为是治标不治本：[krallistic]认为这是对一个“破损系统”的临时修补，指出AI生成内容打破了传统通过文字“证明思考深度”的模式，且可能带来更多问题。

• 担忧该政策带来新的问题：[Balgair]担心此政策可能导致所有研究人员每年固定提交6份申请，反而形成新的“标准”，并可能影响其他基金机构效仿。

• 对AI生成内容的伦理和诚信问题的关注：[bbarnett]强调，使用LLM生成内容如果不加以说明，就是不诚实的行为，并提出应明确规定是否允许使用LLM，以避免学术不端。

• AI生成内容对科研工作的影响：[Al-Khwarizmi]作为科学家，认为LLM可以大大减少撰写基金申请书的时间，尤其是对非英语母语者有帮助，且LLM擅长“夸张的积极语言”，在申请中有优势。因此，他认为科学家使用LLM是合理选择。

• 提出经济手段限制申请：[maratc]建议通过收费的方式限制申请数量，增加经济成本以减少无意义的大量提交。

• 对LLM滥用的技术性解决方案讨论：[d4rkn0d3z]和[tornikeo]提到，面对AI生成的大量低质内容，如何避免“智力拒绝服务攻击”是个技术难题，可能需要类似“垃圾邮件过滤”的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是申请上限的具体数量（6个）是否合理：[nxobject]质疑6个申请的上限如何得出，并担心在资金削减背景下，研究人员可能需要更多申请机会。

• 定性 vs 定量评估标准：[throwpoaster]和[WillQuinn]提到，基金评估应基于“质量”而非“数量”，但在当前复杂政治环境和资金减少的情况下，新政策可能增加研究人员负担。

• AI技术快速发展带来的广泛影响：[sampl3username]批评AI技术公司不负责任地推出新技术，导致诸多“副作用”，包括当前基金申请中出现的问题。

• 最后，有评论（[addicted]）认为，虽然不确定6个申请是否是最合适的数字，但设置限制是必要的，关键在于NIH应密切监控并适时调整政策。

data.title: Roman Roads Research Association (UK)
data.author: countrymile
data.article_summary: 罗马道路研究协会（RRRA）致力于推进对罗马道路网络的研究，尤其受到Ivan D. Margary的著作启发。协会利用现代技术如LiDAR进行研究，揭示 previously 不可见的考古遗迹。协会出版同行评审期刊《Itinera》，专注于罗马道路及交通基础设施的研究，接受会员及非会员投稿。2025年将发布第六卷，涵盖考古发掘报告、LiDAR新发现等内容。协会还举办在线讲座，如Mike Luke和Neil Godfrey等专家的演讲，并计划推出新网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：罗马时代的建筑结构（如步道、道路、运河等）在现代社会中仍然存在并使用，以及现代技术（如LiDAR）在考古发现中的应用。

不同观点：
• mark_undoio认为，现代生活中的许多基础设施，如步道、道路、运河和排水沟，竟然是源于罗马时代建造的，这让人感觉很奇怪。同时，他认为一些罗马时代的建筑可能是基于更早的结构建造的。这里表达了一种对历史遗留影响深刻的感慨，以及对历史层次的思考。

• CharlesXY则将话题引向现代技术，特别是LiDAR技术，认为这种技术对于考古发现非常有用，尤其是在亚马逊雨林这种尚未被完全探索的区域。这表明他对技术推动考古发现充满期待，并暗示了在一些未开发区域可能存在未被发现的古代遗迹。

补充讨论：
• mark_undoio的评论隐含了一种对历史延续性的反思，即古代建筑如何在现代社会中继续发挥作用，并与现代基础设施融为一体。

• CharlesXY的评论则引发了关于技术在考古学中作用的讨论，特别是LiDAR在发现隐藏或未开发区域的潜力，这可能带来新的历史发现。

• 争议的焦点可能在于如何平衡现代技术应用与历史遗迹保护之间的关系，尤其是在未开发或生态敏感区域。

The Roman Roads Research Association was formed to advance knowledge of the Roman road network and promote the study of Roman roads and Roman heritage throughout the British Isles. Our work is inspired by Ivan D. Margary whose âRoman Roads in Britain â (1955) remains the most comprehensive gazetteer ever compiled.
We continue Margaryâs work by researching Roman roads using modern technology such as LiDAR, which uses lasers fired from an aircraft to create an incredibly accurate model of the earthâs surface beneath any vegetation, revealing surviving archaeology otherwise not visible. The example below is a Roman road in Lincolnshire, just east of Grantham, where until recently it was assumed that the A52 followed the course of a Roman road, which it almost certainly doesnât. Instead, a different road leads from the same junction on Ermine Street, apparently serving an entirely local function.

Itinera
is the only journal in the world dedicated to publishing research, fieldwork, and new discoveries that relate to Roman roads or Roman transport infrastructure more broadly, both in Britannia and the rest of the Roman Empire.
We welcome papers which contribute to a better understanding of the road network and its place within the wider context of Roman studies, whether in the UK or internationally.
Itinera includes reports of excavations, new discoveries from lidar, aerial photography, and geophysics, designation of 'new' routes through an expanded Margary system, and a range of peer-
reviewed scholarly articles exploring the wider context of roads as related to military and civilian activity, forts, planning, surveying and all aspects of Roman life. Itinera 6 will include

data.title: The bewildering phenomenon of declining quality
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了现代产品质量和消费模式的变化，指出许多人感觉产品质量下降，如廉价家具、一次性衣物和过度加工食品等。作者引用1976年研究员E. Scott Maynes的观点，认为质量是主观的，取决于消费者的偏好，因此不能绝对地说新产品比旧产品质量更好。专家Javier Carbonell认为，资本主义承诺的“好生活”难以实现，加上社交媒体展示的不可及生活，加剧了这种悲观情绪。文章还提到“效率文化”取代了“紧缩文化”，如特斯拉和Meta等公司通过裁员追求成本最小化。在公共服务方面，如医疗系统，问题在于未能适应社会变化，导致私人保险增加。心理学家Albert Vinyals指出，消费者更看重新颖而非耐用，这种变化在不同代际间产生了分歧。作者总结，老年人更觉质量下降，因他们重视的耐用性已不再被广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品质量是否在下降以及如何评价质量的变化

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如layer8和zkmon）认为产品质量在下降，尤其是成功品牌在市场饱和后为了利润开始偷工减料，导致质量逐渐下滑。他们以个人经历为例，如购买的商品质量不如多年前的旧版本。
• 另一部分用户（如jstummbillig和simianparrot）则认为质量实际上有所提高，但市场上的选择变得更加多样化，消费者可以根据价格和需求选择不同质量层次的商品。他们指出，现在的商品更加注重可负担性、效率和可访问性，这是一种进步。
• raspasov直接对比了过去的诺基亚手机和现代的iPhone，认为现代旗舰手机在各个方面都显著优于旧设备，反驳那些认为过去产品质量更好的观点。
• bitter_michael提出质量的评价标准因人而异，不同消费者对质量有不同的需求和期望，因此不能一概而论。
• weinzierl持中立态度，认为质量的变化在不同领域表现不一，有些产品质量大幅提升（如汽车），而有些则因大众化导致质量下降（如飞机座位）。

补充讨论：
• esperent指出，现代衣物的染色质量比过去更好，质疑那些认为衣物质量下降的观点。

It’s as if the smell of burnt plastic from a dollar store has permeated the world. Things are worse: chipboard furniture, T-shirts unrecognizable after a second wash, packaged foods with more preservatives than ingredients. Airplane seats turned into backrests. Automatic restroom lights that turn off at a whim. But also newspaper articles shamelessly written with
ChatGPT and its algorithmic prose
. Nothing is made to be loved. Only to be bought.
In a study titled

(1976), researcher E. Scott Maynes observed that quality is an inherently subjective concept, as it depends on the preferences of each consumer. Following his reasoning, it cannot be stated in absolute terms that an iPhone 15 is of “better quality” than a 2003 Nokia. For some consumers — although we know there won’t be many — the Nokia’s extreme durability may be more valuable than the iPhone’s technological innovations. Things aren’t worse, they just seem worse to us. But why?
“There is a pessimism that permeates a large part of the population, making everything seem inferior to us,” explains Javier Carbonell, deputy director of
Future Policy Lab
, a think tank focused on designing public policies to combat economic inequalities, over the phone. “This climate affects the judgments we make about the policies implemented and also the products and goods we consume.” According to the expert, the main factor driving this criticism is that the great promise of capitalism — if you work, you can have a decent life, buy a house, and go on vacation —
is no longer being fulfilled
; the social elevator has broken down. “Added to this is the impact of social media, which shows lives unattainable for most people,” he adds.
According to Carbonell, coordinator of the book
La desigualdad en España
(Inequality in Spain)
(2024), the “culture of austerity” that emerged after the Great Recession (2008–2014) has been replaced by a “culture of efficiency,” embodied by Elon Musk, who champions a model aimed at minimizing costs. He first applied it at X (formerly Twitter) — where he laid off more than 75% of the workforce — and later, in the U.S. government.
He’s not alone: Mark Zuckerberg dubbed 2023 the “Year of Efficiency” and carried out massive layoffs at Meta. Amazon, like many other companies, has been gradually replacing human workers with robots and automated systems — to the point that in some of its warehouses, there’s no need to even turn on the lights.
When it comes to public services, the situation is different. Neither the pessimistic climate nor the supposed culture of efficiency alone explain why, between 2017 and 2022, the number of people with private insurance grew by 4% per year. According to the report
The Healthcare System: Current Situation and Future Prospects
, published in 2024, the main reason why Spaniards are turning away from the public healthcare system is the endless waiting lists.
Carbonell argues that, in absolute terms, healthcare services may not be worse than they were a few years ago. “The big problem is that they haven’t adapted to the pace of social change. They haven’t evolved enough to serve the entire elderly population, whose demographic size is increasing every year,” he argues.
Packages of clothing from fast-fashion brand Shein await shipment at a factory in Guangzhou, China, on February 12.

There’s one conclusion that comes up repeatedly throughout this report: the perception that everything is of lower quality is more pronounced among older people. The reasons are varied. The Disordered Consumer)

21 kilograms of clothing per year
, according to the European Environment Agency.

data.title: A 14kb page can load much faster than a 15kb page (2022)
data.author: truxs
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为什么较小的网站加载更快，尤其是14KB的页面可能比15KB的页面快612毫秒，而15KB和16KB之间的差异却很小。这与TCP慢启动算法有关。TCP（传输控制协议）通过确认机制确保数据包完整到达，而慢启动算法用于探测网络能承受的传输量。初始发送的数据量较小，成功后逐渐加倍，直到数据包丢失。通常，服务器从发送10个TCP包开始，每个包1460字节，总计约14KB。如果网站能控制在14KB内，可以减少一次往返时间，显著提升速度。特别是在高延迟的情况下，如卫星互联网，这种差异会非常明显，因为数据传输的物理距离导致延迟较大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页大小优化及其在不同技术环境下的可行性

不同观点：
• [susam] 认为通过自己编写的静态网站生成器和手写HTML、CSS，可以有效控制网页大小，并分享了在使用KaTeX时增加的文件大小。他考虑未来可能采用服务器端渲染来减少客户端资源加载。
• [tonymet] 强调开发者应关注媒体层，指出单个REST请求可能需要多个数据包，且这些数据包需要按顺序到达。他建议通过Chrome开发工具模拟3G模式下的包丢失来测试优化效果。
• [crawshaw] 提出可以通过调整初始窗口(IW)大小来优化网页加载速度，并提到CDN目前设置为30个数据包的初始窗口。
• [GavinAnderegg] 认为将网页大小控制在14kB是一个理想目标，并介绍了一个关注网页大小的项目512kb.club，同时提到Cloudflare Radar工具用于页面大小分析。
• [tgv] 提供了另一个视角，指出在某些地区（如俄罗斯）网络限制使得网页前16KB之后的部分无法加载，强调了小页面大小的重要性。
• [9dev] 认为不了解TCP Slow Start的开发者不需要过于关注网页加载几毫秒的优化，这种优化更适合大公司和有经验的SRE团队。
• [firecall] 分享了自己优化Rails网站的经验，虽然页面大小为17.2KB，但Lighthouse评分达到了100/100。
• [hackerman_fi] 对文章中的两个论点提出质疑，认为没有提供足够的比较数据，且对图片内嵌在初始加载中的情况未作详细说明。
• [Alifatisk] 认为新一代开发者倾向于使用Next.js等框架，而忽略了纯HTML+CSS的简单性。
• [simgt] 强调减少资源消耗以实现可持续发展的重要性，指出网络的环境影响不可忽视。
• [ksec] 认为一致的响应时间比最快的响应时间更重要，提出所有页面应在恰好1秒内完全渲染。
• [the_precipitate] 以老派的视角提到.com文件比.exe文件更节省字节。
• [tomhow] 提到过去讨论过的类似话题，并提供了一个相关链接。
• [mikl] 质疑在支持HTTP/3的现代服务器环境下，14kB的优化建议是否仍然 relevant，因为HTTP/3使用UDP而非TCP。
• [xg15] 指出HTTPS的TLS握手过程会增加多个往返请求，可能超过14kB限制，认为文章建议仅适用于未加密的TCP连接，并提到QUIC/HTTP3可能需要不同的优化策略。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于小页面大小的实际效果和在现代网络技术（如HTTP/3）下的适用性。
• 讨论中还涉及了TLS加密对页面加载优化的影响以及不同网络条件下的实际体验。
• 可持续发展和环境影响也被提出作为优化网页大小的另一个重要考虑因素。

44613625.article_content:
Having a smaller website makes it load faster — that's not surprising.
What is surprising is that
a
14kB
page can load much faster than a
15kB
page
— maybe
612ms
faster — while the difference between a
15kB
and a
16kB
page is trivial.
This is because of the
TCP slow start
algorithm.
This article will cover what that is, how it works, and why you should care.
But first we'll quickly go over some of the basics.
What is TCP?
#
Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
is a way of using the
Internet Protocol (IP)
to send packets of data reliably — sometimes this is referred to as
TCP/IP
.
When a browser requests your website (or an image or a stylesheet) it makes that request using
HTTP
.
HTTP is built on top of TCP and a single HTTP request is usually made up of many TCP
packets
.
On its own IP is just a system for sending packets of data from one location on the internet to another. IP doesn't have a way of checking if a packet has successfully arrived at its destination.
When it comes to websites, knowing that all the data has arrived is important — otherwise we could end up with missing chunks of web page. There are other uses of the web where this doesn't matter so much — like streaming live video.
TCP is an extension of IP that allows a browser and your website's server to tell each other which packets have successfully arrived.
The server sends some packets, then waits for a response from the browser saying it has received the packets (this is called an acknowledgement or ACK), then it sends some more — or if it hasn't received an ACK it can send the packets again.
What is TCP slow start?
#
TCP slow start is an algorithm used by servers to find out how many packets it can send at a time.
When a browser first makes a connection to your server — the server has no way of knowing the amount of
bandwidth
between them.
Bandwidth is how much data can be transmitted over a network per unit of time. Usually it's measured in bits per second (
b/s
). Plumbing is a common analogy — think of bandwidth as how much water can come out of a pipe per second.
Your server doesn't know how much data the connection can handle — so it starts by sending you a small and safe amount of data — usually 10 TCP packets.
If those packets successfully reach your site's visitor, their computer sends back an acknowledgement (ACK) saying the packets have been received.
Your server then sends more data back, but this time it doubles the amount of packets.
This process is repeated until packets are lost and your server doesn't receive an ACK. (At which point the server continues to send packets but at a slower rate).
That's the gist of TCP slow start — in real life the algorithm varies, but that's essentially how it works.
So where does 14kB come from?
#
Most web servers TCP slow start algorithm starts by sending 10 TCP packets.
The maximum size of a TCP packet is
1500 bytes
.
This maximum is not set by the TCP specification, it comes from the
ethernet standard
Each TCP packet uses
40 bytes
in its header —
16 bytes for IP
and an additional
24 bytes for TCP
That leaves
1460 bytes
per TCP packet.
10 x 1460 = 14600 bytes
or roughly 14kB!
So if you can fit your website — or the critical parts of it — into 14kB, you can save visitors a lot of time — the time it takes for one round trip between them and your website's server.
How bad can one round trip be?
#
People are very impatient — and one round trip can be surprisingly long. How long depends on latency…
Latency is the time it takes a packet of data to travel from its source to it's destination.
If bandwidth is how much water can go through a pipe per second — latency is the time it takes a droplet of water to enter the pipe and then exit the other end.
Here's a fun example of how bad latency can be:
Satellite internet
#
Satellite internet is provided by a satellite in orbit around the earth. It's used by people in very unpopulated areas, on oil rigs, cruise ships, and for inflight WiFi on airlines.
To illustrate this example of bad latency, let's imagine a bunch of oil rig bros have forgotten their dice at home and need to use the excellent (under 14kB)
missingdice.com
to play Dungeons & Dragons.
First one of them uses their phone to make a request for the web page…
The
phone
sends that request to the rig's
WiFi router
— which sends that data to the on-rig
satellite dish
— lets be nice and say that takes
1ms
.
The satellite dish then has to send that data to the
satellite
in orbit above the earth.
Typically, this is achieved using a satellite in
geostationary orbit
at
35786km
above the earths surface. The speed of light travels at
299792458 m/s
, so a message sent from earth to the satellite takes
120ms
. The satellite then sends the message back to a
ground station
, which takes another
120ms
.
Then the ground station has to send the request to wherever the
server
is on earth (light slows down to
200000000 m/s
when it's in a fibre optic cable). If the distance between the ground station and the s

不同观点：
• yantrams认为Brahmagupta's identity很有趣，并引用了一个链接，解释了形式为 \(a^2 + n b^2\) 的数在乘法下是封闭的。这表明yantrams对数学恒等式及其性质持有积极的兴趣和欣赏态度。

• QuesnayJr指出，虽然二次型（quadratic forms）听起来简单，但实际上非常复杂。他进一步比较了向优秀高中生解释环上的二次型是可行的，而解释Milnor猜想的证明则对数学研究生来说也是困难的。这显示出QuesnayJr认为数学概念在深度和难度上存在显著差异，强调了数学教育的层次性。

data.title: Occasionally USPS sends me pictures of other people's mail
data.author: shayneo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：USPS的邮件投递问题及其相关服务（如Informed Delivery）的优缺点

不同观点：
• [1a527dd5] 分享了自己长期收到错误邮件的经历，包括银行对账单、购物发票等，最初会联系对方说明情况，但后来选择标记为垃圾邮件。最令人困扰的是收到来自约会网站的邮件。
• [DamnInteresting] 提到使用Informed Delivery服务时，USPS会推送与实际邮件无关的电子 junk mail，例如播客更新，且无法单独选择退出这些通知。
• [duxup] 提到自己曾频繁收到邻居的邮件，虽然最近几年情况有所改善，但使用Informed Delivery后因邮件延迟到达引发不必要的担忧。
• [ews] 提到USPS开始发送关于自己几年前住址的邮件图片，且无法停止这些邮件。
• [jchw] 认为收到他人邮件并不罕见，且通常不会造成大问题，因为邮政系统偶尔会出错，但不意味着存在重大隐患。
• [mv4] 指出自己的情况是由于街道地址数字混淆导致收到错误邮件，比如将"0"误认为"8"。
• [supernova87a] 深入讨论了地址系统的复杂性，提出许多潜在问题，如公寓单元号的缺失、地址细微差异等，认为邮政系统和金融机构在处理地址时可能面临巨大挑战。
• [PopePompus] 提到自己持续收到前屋主的邮件图片，认为这涉及隐私泄露，尤其是前屋主似乎在家中经营生意。
• [somehnguy] 指出邮件信封有时可以被看穿，存在潜在隐私风险。
• [jasonthorsness] 首次了解到Informed Delivery服务，认为即使偶尔看到别人的邮件也无所谓，整体服务仍然很有价值。
• [jabroni_salad] 分享了自己将重要邮件退回发件人并标记条形码的经验，认为Informed Delivery系统使用光学识别，而分拣系统使用条形码，导致问题发生。
• [mNovak] 提到自己住在公寓，经常收到前住户的邮件，但这些邮件实际上不会被投递，认为Informed Delivery系统存在捕捉错误邮件的机制。
• [seiferteric] 提到曾通过USPS网站报告问题并得到解决，但系统问题仍然存在。
• [GauntletWizard] 认为偶尔收到他人邮件是处理实体邮件时的正常不确定性，不认为这是一个漏洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Informed Delivery服务的实用性与缺陷。部分用户认为该服务带来便利，而另一些用户则因收到无关推送或他人邮件而感到困扰。
• 邮件投递错误的具体原因多样，包括地址混淆、公寓单元号缺失、前住户未更新地址等，反映了邮政系统在处理地址时的复杂性。
• 隐私问题被多次提及，尤其是当用户收到涉及他人敏感信息的邮件时，如银行对账单、购物发票等。
• 部分用户提到通过联系USPS解决问题，但效果不一，有些问题仍未得到彻底解决。

data.title: We made Postgres writes faster, but it broke replication
data.author: philippemnoel
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了在优化Postgres写入速度时遇到的问题及其解决方案。为了提升Postgres的全文搜索吞吐量，团队采用了LSM树（Log-Structured Merge Tree）这种写优化数据结构，显著提高了写入性能。然而，这种优化却破坏了Postgres的物理复制机制。

LSM树通过将随机写入转换为顺序写入来提升性能，但在复制过程中，Postgres的物理复制（基于WAL日志传输）无法保证LSM树的复制安全性，导致数据不一致。团队发现，物理一致性并不等同于逻辑一致性，后者要求副本数据反映主数据库的稳定视图。

为解决此问题，团队利用了Postgres的`hot_standby_feedback`设置，并探讨了WAL日志传输如何保证物理一致性，以及为何需要原子性来确保逻辑一致性。最终，通过深入分析和调整，团队成功修复了复制问题，确保了LSM树在Postgres中的复制安全性。

主要讨论点：关于技术内容深度的评价及其实现细节的讨论，尤其是与WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）和Postgres相关的问题。

不同观点：
• [timetoogo] 认为这种无冗余的技术深度内容非常值得推荐，尤其是在Hacker News（HN）上需要更多类似的内容。
• [kikimora] 赞同需要更多深度内容，但对WAL和内存中锁如何影响WAL传输提出疑问。具体讨论了WAL的读写机制，并质疑是否需要在块级别上进行原子操作。同时，提出使用自定义存储引擎可能比在Postgres上进行复杂操作更有效，暗示现有实现可能导致大量死元组（dead tuples）产生，增加了维护难度。
• [otterley] 对使用自定义方案替代Elasticsearch或OpenSearch表示质疑，认为现有工具已经足够，没有必要重新发明轮子，并用“锤子和拇指”作比喻，暗示过度工程化的问题。

补充讨论：
• [truetraveller] 提出了关于图表制作方式的简单问题，未涉及更深层次的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否应该使用现有的成熟工具（如Elasticsearch、OpenSearch）还是开发自定义解决方案。
• 另一个争议点是关于Postgres中WAL和锁机制的复杂性，以及是否应该通过自定义存储引擎来解决相关问题。

44633933.article_content:
Previous Post
Next Post
We Made Postgres Writes Faster, but it Broke Replication
+2
By Stu Hood, Ming Ying, Mathew Pregasen, and Olive Ratliff on June 30, 2025
When we built
pg_search
, the Postgres extension for search and analytics, write throughput was a priority. To be an effective alternative to Elasticsearch we needed to support high ingest workloads in real time.
This is because many Elasticsearch use cases — like real-time dashboards, e-commerce search, and recommendation systems — involve continuous writes that must be indexed and made searchable immediately.
In a vanilla Postgres implementation, full-text search is backed by a
B-tree
or
GIN
(Generalized Inverted Index) structure. These indexes are good for relatively fast lookups, but they aren’t so fast for writes.
We opted for a data structure optimized for writes: a
Log-Structured Merge (
LSM
) tree
. That was great for write throughput, but it broke Postgres replication! Specifically, it broke physical replication, one of the two mechanisms that allow Postgres to replicate data from a primary node across one or more read replicas.
The other mode is logical replication, which sends individual row changes to replicas instead of copying the database byte-for-byte.
It turned out that Postgres's out-of-the-box support for physical replication, built on Write-Ahead Log (WAL) shipping, isn't quite enough for an advanced data structure like an LSM tree to be replication-safe. We were surprised to learn this, so we decided to write up our experience and describe how we fixed the problem.
In this post, we'll do a deep dive into:
What is an LSM tree?
What it means for an LSM tree to be replication-safe
How Postgres' WAL shipping guarantees physical consistency
Why atomic logging was necessary for logical consistency
How we leveraged a little-known but powerful Postgres setting called
hot_standby_feedback
What is an LSM Tree?
A Log-Structured Merge Tree (LSM tree) is a write-optimized data structure commonly used in systems like RocksDB and Cassandra.
The core idea behind an LSM tree is to turn random writes into sequential ones. Incoming writes are first stored in an in-memory buffer called a memtable, which is fast to update. Once the memtable fills up, it is flushed to disk as a sorted, immutable segment file (often called an SSTable).
These segment files are organized by size into layers or levels. Newer data is written to the topmost layer. Over time, data is gradually pushed down into lower levels through a process called compaction, where data from smaller segments is
merged, deduplicated, and rewritten into larger segments.
What Do We Mean by Replication Safety?
A reliable distributed datastore (one which guarantees “replication safety”) must demonstrate both
physical
and
logical
consistency
1
2
across database replicas.
Physical consistency
means the replica contains structurally valid data — each page or block on disk is well-formed and corresponds to a state that did exist on the primary at some point.
Logical consistency
ensures that the data on the replica reflects a coherent and stable view of the database, something that could have been seen by a transaction on the primary.
A physically consistent state is
not
always a logically consistent state. Specifically, if you take a snapshot of a physically consistent replica while replicating an in-flight transaction, it may not be logically consistent.
A good analogy is to imagine replicating a book. Physical consistency is like copying every page exactly, even if you're in the middle of a chapter — you're guaranteed to have real pages, but you might end up with half a sentence or a missing footnote.
Logical consistency is like waiting until the chapter is finished before copying it, ensuring the result makes sense to a reader.
WAL Shipping: How Postgres Guarantees Physical Consistency
In a primary-standby physical replication setup, a primary server is paired with a standby server that acts as a read-only copy of its leader. The servers remain in sync by using a Write-Ahead Log (WAL) to record all binary-level changes to storage blocks on the primary server before they occur. Changes to this append-only WAL file are then streamed to the standby (a process called “log shipping”) and applied in the order received. This process enables near-realtime data synchronization between the two servers, hence the phrase “hot standby”.
Why Atomicity is a Requirement for Physical Consistency
Atomicity is a requirement for physical consistency because Postgres locks are not replayed on replica servers. This is because replaying every lock taken on the primary would require strict timing synchronization, significantly impacting performance and hindering the ability of the standby to serve reads. Instead, the WAL uses per-buffer locks to incrementally replay edits in some particular order: it acquires an exclusive lock on the buffer (the in-memory representation of a block), makes its change, and then releases it

data.title: TrackWeight: Turn your MacBook's trackpad into a digital weighing scale
data.author: wtcactus
data.article_summary: TrackWeight是一款macOS应用，通过利用MacBook触控板的Force Touch压力传感器，将其变成一个精准的数字秤。该应用使用Takuto Nakamura的Open Multi-Touch Support库来获取详细的压力数据，并通过校准将其转换为重量测量。使用时，用户需将手指放在触控板上，同时将物体轻置于触控板上以获取读数。该应用要求macOS 13.0及以上版本、配备Force Touch的MacBook、禁用App Sandbox，以及Xcode 16.0和Swift 6.0用于开发。由于需要手指接触，金属物体可能需要隔开以获得准确读数。该项目基于SwiftUI和Combine构建，并附带MIT许可证，但仅用于实验和教育目的，不建议用于关键测量或商业应用。

TrackWeight
Turn your MacBook's trackpad into a precise digital weighing scale
TrackWeight
is a macOS application that transforms your MacBook's trackpad into an accurate weighing scale by leveraging the Force Touch pressure sensors built into modern MacBook trackpads.
IMG_7303.mov
To use it yourself:
Open the scale
Rest your finger on the trackpad
While mainting finger contact, put your object on the trackpad
Try and put as little pressure on the trackpad while still maintaining contact. This is the weight of your object
How It Works
TrackWeight utilizes the
Open Multi-Touch Support library
by
Takuto Nakamura
to gain private access to all mouse and trackpad events on macOS. This library provides detailed touch data including pressure readings that are normally inaccessible to standard applications.
The key insight is that trackpad pressure events are only generated when there's capacitance detected on the trackpad surface - meaning your finger (or another conductive object) must be in contact with the trackpad. When this condition is met, the trackpad's Force Touch sensors provide precise pressure readings that can be calibrated and converted into weight measurements.
Calibration Process
The weight calculations have been validated by:
Placing the MacBook trackpad directly on top of a conventional digital scale
Applying various known weights while maintaining finger contact with the trackpad
Comparing and calibrating the pressure readings against the reference scale measurements
Ensuring consistent accuracy across different weight ranges
It turns out that the data we get from MultitouchSupport is already in grams!
Requirements
macOS 13.0+
(for Open Multi-Touch Support library compatibility)
MacBook with Force Touch trackpad
(2015 or newer MacBook Pro, 2016 or newer MacBook)
App Sandbox disabled
(required for low-level trackpad access)
Xcode 16.0+
and
Swift 6.0+
(for development)
Installation
Clone this repository
Open
TrackWeight.xcodeproj
in Xcode
Disable App Sandbox in the project settings (required for trackpad access)
Build and run the application
Limitations
Finger contact required
: The trackpad only provides pressure readings when it detects capacitance (finger touch), so you cannot weigh objects directly without maintaining contact
Surface contact
: Objects being weighed must be placed in a way that doesn't interfere with the required finger contact
Metal objects
: Metal objects may be detected as a finger touch, so you may need to place a piece of paper or a cloth between the object and the trackpad to get an accurate reading
Technical Details
The application is built using:
SwiftUI
for the user interface
Combine
for reactive data flow
Open Multi-Touch Support library
for low-level trackpad access
Open Multi-Touch Support Library
This project relies heavily on the excellent work by
Takuto Nakamura
(
@Kyome22
) and the
Open Multi-Touch Support library
. The library provides:
Access to global multitouch events on macOS trackpads
Detailed touch data including position, pressure, angle, and density
Thread-safe async/await support for touch event streams
Touch state tracking and comprehensive sensor data
License

Disclaimer
This application is for experimental and educational purposes. While efforts have been made to ensure accuracy, TrackWeight should not be used for critical measurements or commercial applications where precision is essential. Always verify measurements with a calibrated scale for important use cases.

data.title: UK backing down on Apple encryption backdoor after pressure from US
data.author: azalemeth
data.article_summary: 英国政府在要求苹果公司提供访问安全客户数据的权限上，面临与特朗普政府的对抗。两名英国高级官员表示，英国内政部可能迫于华盛顿的压力而让步。内政部根据《调查权力法》要求苹果创建后门访问其最安全的云存储，苹果则在今年二月撤回了该服务并提起法律挑战。美国副总统JD Vance及特朗普等高层对英国的加密技术处理表示不满，认为这可能影响两国科技合作。与此同时，英国政府正在寻求解决方案，避免进一步激化矛盾，尤其是在人工智能和数据合作方面。

Sir Keir Starmer’s government is seeking a way out of a clash with the Trump administration over the UK’s demand that Apple provide it with access to secure customer data, two senior British officials have told the Financial Times.
The officials both said the Home Office, which ordered the tech giant in January to grant access to its most secure cloud storage system, would probably have to retreat in the face of pressure from senior leaders in Washington, including Vice President JD Vance.
“This is something that the vice president is very annoyed about and which needs to be resolved,” said an official in the UK’s technology department. “The Home Office is basically going to have to back down.”
Both officials said the UK decision to force Apple to break its end-to-end encryption—which has been raised multiple times by top officials in Donald Trump’s administration—could impede technology agreements with the US.
“One of the challenges for the tech partnerships we’re working on is the encryption issue,” the first official said. “It’s a big red line in the US—they don’t want us messing with their tech companies.”
Starmer’s government has set out a trade strategy that focuses on digital goals such as AI and data partnerships.
The other senior government official added that the Home Office had handled the issue of Apple encryption very badly and now had “its back against the wall,” adding: “It’s a problem of the Home Office’s own making, and they’re working on a way around it now.”
In its order in January, the Home Office told Apple to build in a “back door” to allow law enforcement or security services to tap into the cloud storage system that stores user data that even the iPhone maker itself is currently unable to access.
It did so by issuing a “technical capability notice” under the UK Investigatory Powers Act, legislation that critics dub a “snooper’s charter” but that the government maintains is needed by law enforcement to investigate terrorism and child sexual abuse.
Under the terms of the legislation, recipients of such a notice are unable to discuss the matter publicly, even with customers affected by the order, unless granted permission by the Home Secretary.
The legislation’s use against Apple has triggered the tech industry’s highest-profile battle over encryption technology in almost a decade.
In response to the demand, Apple withdrew its most secure cloud storage service from the UK in February and is now challenging the Home Office’s order at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal, which probes complaints against the UK’s security services.
Last month, Meta-owned WhatsApp said it would join Apple’s legal challenge, in a rare collaboration between the Silicon Valley rivals.
In the meantime, the Home Office continues to pursue its case with Apple at the tribunal.
Its lawyers discussed the next legal steps this month, reflecting the divisions within government over how best to proceed. “At this point, the government has not backed down,” said one person familiar with the legal process.
A third senior British official added that the UK government was reluctant to push “anything that looks to the US vice-president like a free-speech issue.”
In a combative speech at the Munich Security Conference in February, Vance argued that free speech and democracy were threatened by European elites.
The UK official added, this “limits what we’re able to do in the future, particularly in relation to AI regulation.” The Labour government has delayed plans for AI legislation until after May next year.
Trump has also been critical of the UK stance on encryption.
The US president has likened the UK’s order to Apple to “something... that you hear about with China,” saying in February that he had told Starmer: “You can’t do this.”
US Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard has also suggested the order would be an “egregious violation” of Americans’ privacy that risked breaching the two countries’ data agreement.
Apple did not respond to a request for comment. “We have never built a back door or master key to any of our products, and we never will,” Apple said in February.
The UK government did not respond to a request for comment.
A spokesperson for Vance declined to comment.
The Home Office has previously said the UK has “robust safeguards and independent oversight to protect privacy” and that these powers “are only used on an exceptional basis, in relation to the most serious crimes.”

data.title: Shale Drillers Turn on Each Other as Toxic Water Leaks Hit Biggest US Oil Field
data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：水力压裂（fracking）的环境影响、监管问题以及其在地缘政治和能源结构中的角色。

不同观点：
• **水力压裂的环境与健康影响**：[tomrod]和[jasonephraim]分享了关于压裂化学品泄漏和污染的实地经验和研究，强调了水污染的普遍性以及报告不充分的问题。他们指出，许多化学品由于商业秘密未被报告，且有证据显示附近居民的健康受到威胁，如儿童白血病风险增加。[mistersquid]通过YouTube视频展示了压裂导致的地下水可燃问题，引发了公众震惊。

• **地缘政治与能源结构的讨论**：[sgt101]从地缘政治角度分析了美国石油生产的巅峰与衰退将带来的全球影响，指出可再生能源和核能如果不能填补石油缺口，美国将面临军事和经济挑战。该评论强调了导弹技术进步和竞争对手崛起对美国全球主导地位的威胁。

• **可再生能源与化石燃料的比较**：[bickfordb]对公众仍然支持压裂而不是选择太阳能和风能表示惊讶，暗示了对化石燃料的依赖与清洁能源发展之间的矛盾。[jeffbee]则通过对比压裂与风力发电废弃物问题，批评了反对可再生能源的论点。

• **水资源使用的争议**：[billfor]质疑水力压裂的水资源消耗问题，认为与高尔夫球场相比，压裂井的用水量未必过大，这一观点与[tomrod]和[jasonephraim]对环境影响的担忧形成对比。

补充讨论：
• **监管与公众参与的失败**：[jasonephraim]详细描述了在科罗拉多州反对压裂项目的艰难过程，指出尽管有大量公众反对和证据显示环境与健康风险，监管机构仍批准项目。他还提到，在项目审批过程中存在透明度不足和程序违规的问题。

• **讽刺与批评**：[chiffre01]用“钻吧，宝贝，钻吧”讽刺了继续推动压裂的态度，暗示了对能源政策的不满。[jeffbee]则通过具体文章批评了对风力发电废弃物问题的夸大。

争议的焦点主要集中在压裂对环境和健康的实际影响、监管的有效性以及可再生能源与化石燃料之间的选择。

data.title: Spanish police arrest five over $542M crypto investment scheme
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 2025年6月，西班牙国民警卫队和欧洲刑警组织联合开展"Borrelli行动"，逮捕了五名涉嫌参与国际加密货币投资诈骗的人员。该团伙通过位于马德里和加那利群岛的网络同伙，以现金存款、电汇和加密货币交易等方式，从全球超过5,000名受害者处洗钱约4.6亿欧元（约5.42亿美元）。他们利用位于香港的一家公司，伪装成合法外汇投资企业，诱骗受害者进行虚假加密货币投资。该团伙使用复杂的空壳公司和银行账户网络，以及虚假身份注册的加密货币账户，掩盖非法资金来源。调查始于2023年，目前仍在进行中。此类诈骗是全球最昂贵的网络欺诈形式之一，尤其在东南亚地区日益猖獗。

Personnel from Spain's Guardia Civil and Europol participate in Operation Borrelli in June 2025. Image: Guardia Civil via Europol
Daryna Antoniuk
July 1st, 2025
Spanish police arrest five over $542 million crypto investment scheme
Spanish law enforcement arrested five people suspected of running an international cryptocurrency investment fraud scheme that laundered more than €460 million ($542 million) from over 5,000 victims worldwide, according to a
statement
from Europol.
The suspects, based in Madrid and the Canary Islands, allegedly operated a global network of accomplices who collected money through cash deposits, wire transfers and cryptocurrency transactions.
According to Spain’s Guardia Civil, the criminal ring
used
a company based in Hong Kong, posing as a legitimate foreign-exchange investment firm, to lure victims into bogus crypto deals.
The arrests were carried out last week as part of an operation codenamed Borrelli. Authorities believe the network used a complex web of shell companies and bank accounts across multiple countries, as well as crypto exchange accounts registered under false or borrowed identities, to disguise the origin of the illicit funds.
The investigation began in 2023 and remains ongoing. Neither Europol or the Guardia Civil offered details about the scheme’s potential connections to known crime networks.
Cryptocurrency investment scams remain one of the costliest forms of online fraud globally. The FBI
said
Americans lost more than $5.8 billion to such schemes last year alone. Earlier in June, the U.S. Department of Justice announced efforts to recover over $225 million in cryptocurrency stolen through confidence and romance scams run out of Vietnam and the Philippines.
In May, the U.S. Treasury
sanctioned
Philippines-based infrastructure firm Funnull Technology Inc. for supporting hundreds of thousands of websites tied to so-called “pig butchering” scams —  fraud operations that combine social engineering, fake investment pitches, and romance lures to drain victims’ crypto wallets.
Such scams are fueling a growing illicit cybercrime economy in Southeast Asia, where transnational criminal groups, shell companies, gambling networks, and scam compounds increasingly collaborate across borders.

44635403.article_summary: 2025年6月，西班牙国民警卫队和欧洲刑警组织联合开展"Borrelli行动"，逮捕了五名涉嫌参与国际加密货币投资诈骗的人员。该团伙通过位于马德里和加那利群岛的网络同伙，以现金存款、电汇和加密货币交易等方式，从全球超过5,000名受害者处洗钱约4.6亿欧元（约5.42亿美元）。他们利用位于香港的一家公司，伪装成合法外汇投资企业，诱骗受害者进行虚假加密货币投资。该团伙使用复杂的空壳公司和银行账户网络，以及虚假身份注册的加密货币账户，掩盖非法资金来源。调查始于2023年，目前仍在进行中。此类诈骗是全球最昂贵的网络欺诈形式之一，尤其在东南亚地区日益猖獗。

data.title: Please, FOSS world, we need something like ChromeOS
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 文章呼吁开源社区开发一个像ChromeOS一样简单易用的操作系统，以替代即将停止支持的Windows 10。作者强调，ChromeOS通过简化的Linux系统让旧电脑轻松上网，且无需谷歌账户，这正是许多非Linux用户所需要的。尽管Linux发行版众多，但过多的选择反而让人困扰。ChromeOS通过仅提供基本功能，如浏览器和简单文件管理器，实现了高度的简洁和稳定性，甚至可以在无技术支持的情况下大规模销售。其双根分区设计和基于镜像的更新使其具备高度容错能力。文章提到，若谷歌停止开发ChromeOS，类似FydeOS和NayuOS的项目也可能受到影响。作者希望开源社区能创造出一个无需额外账户、极简且免费的操作系统。

44635640.article_content:
OSes
13
Please, FOSS world, we need something like ChromeOS
13
The End of Windows 10 is looming. The world needs a simpler, easy, quick, snackable alternative
Liam Proven
Mon 21 Jul 2025
//
14:05 UTC
Comment
Dear Santa. For
Windows-10-end-of-support-day
in October, please may we have a dead simple bulletproof all-free OS that gets old PCs online without a Google account, and does nothing else?
There are a lot of desktop Linux distros out there. It's the number one thing non-Linux users complain about: too much choice. One of them only comes bundled with hardware, and yet, it has
more users than all the others
. It's ChromeOS, and it
could be facing the chop soon
. How come there is no all-Free Software tool that even tries to do what ChromeOS does
without
needing an account with The Borg?
Even if it may soon be replaced by a desktop flavor of Android, ChromeOS does just one thing and it does it well enough that vendors sold
billions of the things
last year.
The idea of ChromeOS is simple: it's just enough Linux to get you online. It turns a PC into something akin to a tablet, with a full-screen icon-based app launcher. The desktop is very simple and vaguely Windows-like: there's a taskbar at the bottom, a file manager, drivers enough common hardware that most things just work out of the box, including a bunch of common GPUs, networking including Wi-Fi. In terms of apps, there's a built-in Google Drive client, and of course the Chrome web browser.
And that is about it. Anything else that you want to do, you do in a browser window. Productivity apps? Use Google Apps. Messaging or video calling? Log in to your chat system of choice in a browser window. The file manager can show images, but not much more. Your bookmarks, passwords, and what few settings there are are stored in your Google account.
All the components are there, including a potential revenue model. Strip out absolutely all the complexity that can possibly be removed, and leave something which can run on any old PC from the last 15 years and gets the user online – and nothing else. How hard can it be?
There are no optional extra native apps, and no way to add any. If you have branded ChromeBook hardware, there's the Google Play store and it can run some Android apps in a built-in compatibility environment. Around the Irish Sea division of Vulture Towers, we mostly just use ChromeOS Flex on whatever spare laptop is lying around, which works very nicely indeed. There's no app store, but you can open a Debian VM and install Debian apps in there. We installed VLC so that it could play movies or audio files, and it automatically integrated with the desktop – suddenly, clicking on a movie in the file manager just worked.
This is the sort of simplicity that we feel a desktop Linux for the masses should aspire to. There are no local apps and no questions: no choice of desktop, no dual boot, no fancy add-on cross-distro package managers like Flatpak or Snap. The desktop is just Windows-like enough to be instantly familiar, unlike GNOME; on the flipside, it's not cluttered with a hundred options to tweak, plus two Help/About menu entries, three text editors, menu bars in some apps and hamburger menus in others, as in KDE Plasma.
Where Google's team put innovative effort into ChromeOS was in making it robust enough to be sold to the masses in the hundreds of millions of units, with
no tech support.
It's immutable, with image-based updates. It has two root partitions, one of which updates the other, so there's always a known good one to fall back to if an update should fail.
This is a more fault-tolerant design than SUSE's MicroOS-based systems, which use the rather fragile Btrfs. It's also much simpler than the
Fedora Atomic
immutable systems, including offshoots such as
Universal Blue
, which use the Git-like — for which, read "fearsomely complex" —
OSTree
. For added entertainment, Fedora also defaults to Btrfs, with compression enabled. If you don't believe us about the problems of damaged Btrfs volumes, refer to
the Btrfs documentation
. We recommend taking the orange-highlighted
Warning
section
very
seriously indeed.
It seems to us like there's nothing to rival this in the non-Google world. There have been ready-rolled web-kiosk OSes such as
Webconverger
. It was
open source
, based on Debian, with
updated over Git
. It was end-of-lifed a couple of years ago.
Like Chrome itself, the upstream project behind ChromeOS,
ChromiumOS
, is open source. There are a couple of projects forked from the basis of ChromiumOS, such as
FydeOS
, which adds a second authentication system so it can be used behind the Great Firewall of China. We plan to return to FydeOS and take a deeper look soon.
NayuOS
is comparable: it's broadly ChromiumOS, with some added tools for developers. It's mainly intended for use in guest-login mode, but it can also talk to
Nexedi's SlapOS
back-end servers.
If Mountain View
does
decide to stop developing ChromeOS, expect both of these to stop

data.title: Cryptocurrency exchanges begin offering tokenized securities
data.author: doodaddy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加密token化的证券及其创新、风险和争议

不同观点：
• **seanhunter**：认为加密token化的证券创新在于将存托凭证（depositary receipt）转换为加密token。存托凭证早已存在，用于让股票在原上市国家以外的市场交易，增加流动性。这种做法有税收和其他优势，例如不需要报告外汇损益。
• **toenail**：质疑token化证券的合法性，认为如果法官可以判定证券属于某一方而非token持有者，那么token化证券就毫无意义，它们可能只是数据库记录。
• **dreamcompiler**：指出客户可能会使用稳定币购买这些token化证券，但稳定币具有非波动性，直到其价值在几分钟内跌至零。
• **lxgr**：认为在美国，几乎每个人都可以开设证券账户并获得SIPC保险等保护。然而，公开可投资的股市在整体美国公司中的比例越来越小。除非token化证券能让非合格投资者接触到私人投资，否则这个创新并没有解决关键问题。
• **yk**：简单将token化证券类比为股票的NFT，表达对两者相似性的疑惑。
• **lvl155**：对加密社区的创新持批评态度，认为这些是新的骗局和陷阱。
• **Jessibot**：提到token化证券的支持者认为这将打破让富人受益的壁垒，使交易更便宜、透明和易于大众参与。但批评者担心这会破坏一个世纪以来的证券法和投资者保护。加密领域中证券的定义本身也是一个有争议的问题，例如2021年Binance因德国监管机构的要求撤回了token化证券产品。
• **FollowingTheDao**：引用支持者的说法，即token化能让普通人成为“鲸鱼”，但实际上通过费用剥削投资者。
• **richwater**：认为整个token化证券的趋势最终会像荷兰的郁金香泡沫一样崩溃。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于token化证券是否真的能为投资者提供更多机会和便利，还是只是新的金融泡沫和骗局。
• 合法性和监管问题也是讨论的重点，特别是在加密领域中证券定义的模糊性和各国监管的不确定性。
• 稳定币的潜在风险也被提及，特别是其非波动性可能带来的价值突然崩溃的风险。

data.title: I've launched 37 products in 5 years and not doing that again
data.author: AlexandrBel
data.article_summary: 作者AlexBelogubov分享了自己在推出37个产品后的经验。他发现，虽然只有一个产品走红，但大多数产品并非失败，只是增长缓慢。他的当前项目Refgrow经历了六个月才获得首位付费客户，但现在稳步增长，且几乎无需营销预算。他总结，专注于一个项目并持续改进，往往比不断追逐新产品更易获得稳定成果。他提问其他开发者是否通过专注和耐心取得成功，还是依靠大量推出新产品，并希望听取他人的经验和建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创业和产品开发中的市场适应、执行力、多项目策略与专注单一项目的争议

不同观点：
• **nzach** 认为，许多创业社区过度强调市场适应，而忽视了产品执行和创意本身的价值。他分享了自己花费大量精力开发产品却收到泛泛的建议，感到失望。他主张鼓励人们开发有趣的产品，即使其商业化前景不明。

• **shahzaibmushtaq** 分享了自己的成功经验，通过一个病毒式传播的产品获得了六位数的收入，并指出那些未能成功的产品是因为采取了“只要建好了，他们就会来”的错误营销方式。这表明市场适应和营销策略的重要性。

• **forgotmypw17** 强调了耐心与多项目并行的好处，认为既要专注于一个项目，也要同时发展多个项目，这样可以在等待中积累经验和知识。

• **rorylaitila** 批评了所谓的“霰弹枪资本主义”，即不断尝试新项目而不深耕任何一个的做法，认为这是对时间和资源的浪费。他主张基于反馈和能力进行合理的扩展。

• **Invictus0** 批评了 indie hacker 社区中大量开发无意义小工具的现象，主张与客户交谈，专注于解决一个具体问题，逐步成长。

补充讨论：
• **GianFabien** 对六位数销售收入的真实价值提出了质疑，指出在扣除费用和税收后，这样的收入可能仅够作为副业，不足以替代常规收入。

• **reactordev** 和 **bob1029** 对大量开发新项目的可行性表示怀疑，前者因烧光了自己的精力而转向咨询工作，后者对37个产品的数量表示怀疑，认为这可能是在夸大其词。

争议焦点：创业者应专注于一个项目深耕细作，还是应多项目并行以寻找突破点，以及产品开发中市场适应与执行力的相对重要性。

After launching 37 different products over the last few years, I’ve had one go viral and almost all the others struggle to get any traction at all.
Like many indie makers, I used to think the best strategy was to just keep launching, make more bets, and hope one finally catches fire.
But here’s what I’ve learned:
Virality is rare and nearly impossible to predict
Most of my launches that failed didn’t actually fail, they just grew much slower than I expected
My current project,
Refgrow

data.title: What happens when housing prices go down?
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：住房市场的供需关系、价格变化的影响以及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• rwarfield认为文章逻辑混乱，自相矛盾。文章声称房价在一些城市已经开始下跌，但随后又提到这些城市房价上涨最快。他还指出，作者混淆了供应曲线和供应量的概念，并批评作者提出的“小规模、渐进式开发”增加供应的建议没有解释清楚为何不会导致负面经济影响。

• eviks指出，文章错误地理解了因果关系。房价下跌是否会让建筑商和贷款方紧张，取决于导致价格下跌的原因。高利率和材料成本波动等问题并不能通过加快许可证审批来缓解。

• Bluescreenbuddy提到在芝加哥，一些地方议员试图增加建筑项目，但遇到老年房主的反对，这反映了地方层面的阻力。

• Workaccount2用泰勒·斯威夫特演唱会门票的例子来说明住房市场的供需问题，指出增加座位数量可能降低体验质量，并提出如何平衡不同层次需求的问题。

• stego-tech认为住房问题反映了更大的经济结构性问题，核心在于经济利益集团不愿改变现状，而工人阶级则希望改革。他主张通过提高工资和实施价格控制来应对高价格，但指出这在当前政治经济环境下难以实现。

• yoden认为价格下跌不一定会导致供应减少，当前市场的扭曲是由于政府监管和开发商、地主的利益驱动。

• spicybbq指出，价格下跌导致供应减少是合理的，因为供应商会根据价格变化调整供应，而不是在价格下跌时增加供应。

• queenkjuul强调NIMBY（"不要建在我家后院"）主义者的反对使得合理的政策难以推行，认为只有社会住房才是有效的解决方案。

• rossdavidh提到，尽管住房被当作金融产品对待是一个问题，但在一些州房价已经开始下跌，如佛罗里达和德克萨斯，因此认为“不允许房价下跌”的说法并不完全正确。

• JJMcJ指出，解决房价下跌和政治需求矛盾的常见方法是让人们接受长通勤距离，并回顾了2008年后房价下跌的历史。

• Akranazon认为，建造和贷款的根本目的应该是让住房更加负担得起，而不是保护相关方的利润，因此对建筑商和贷款方在价格下跌时紧张的反应不以为然。

• roenxi认为，现实中房价下跌不被庆祝是因为没有政治话语权的人被忽略。文章中关于价格下跌导致供应减少的说法是悖论，因为如果价格低意味着更多人有了住房，那么新的建筑就可能不必要。

• btbuildem指出，当前的激励机制与公开宣称的建造更多住房的目标不一致，开发商的主要目的是赚钱而非提供住房。

• projektfu批评文章在提到达拉斯房价时自相矛盾，前文说房价下跌，后文又说房价飙升。

• ajsnigrutin认为，只要人们愿意支付高于土地、政府成本、材料和劳动成本的总和，住房就会继续建造。他指出，政府政策和金融市场是导致房价高企的主要原因。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于房价下跌是否会导致供应减少，以及如何在保持经济稳定的同时增加住房供应。
- 讨论还涉及NIMBY主义对政策推行的阻力，以及更广泛的经济结构性问题如何影响住房市场。
- 一些评论者强调了政府政策和金融市场的角色，认为这些是解决住房问题的关键。

data.title: A circle and a hyperbola living in one plot
data.author: tobytylam
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了一个含有复数单位 \(i\) 的三维方程 \(x^2 + (y + zi)^2 = 1\) 的几何意义，并通过分解实部和虚部发现它包含一个圆和一个双曲线。具体来说：

1. 方程展开后得到：
   - 实部：\(x^2 + y^2 - z^2 = 1\)
   - 虚部：\(yz = 0\)

2. 根据 \(yz = 0\)，分两种情况讨论：
   - \(y = 0\) 时，得到双曲线 \(x^2 - z^2 = 1\)
   - \(z = 0\) 时，得到圆 \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\)

文章进一步解释了这种几何图形与实矩阵复特征值的关系。例如，对于矩阵 \(M(\mu) = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1+\mu \\ 1-\mu & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)，其特征值满足 \(\mu^2 + \lambda^2 = 1\)，这与前面的几何图形一致。通过图形可以直观地观察特征值的行为，如复特征值和实特征值的转换。

最后，文章还分析了另一个矩阵的例子，展示了类似的几何分析方法。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44604149.article_content:
We will see that the 3D plot of \(x^2 + (y + zi)^2 = 1\), where \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) are real and \(i\) is the imaginary unit, contains both a circle and a hyperbola. This visualization sheds light on the complex eigenvalues of real matrices.
Let’s start by expanding the equation \(x^2+(y+zi)^2 = 1\) and separating it into real and imaginary parts. We get:
\[\begin{align*}
&\text{Real Part:} &x^2 + y^2 - z^2 &= 1, \\
&\text{Imaginary Part:} &yz &= 0.
\end{align*}\]
The condition \(yz=0\) splits into two cases:
\[\begin{align*}
\text{Case 1: }y&=0 \text{ and so } x^2-z^2 = 1\\
\text{Case 2: }z&=0 \text{ and so } x^2+y^2 = 1
\end{align*}\]
Case 1 nets us a hyperbola in the \(xz\)-plane. Case 2 nets us a unit circle in the \(xy\)-plane.
You can check out the plot at
desmos
.
Eigenvalues and dynamical systems
Why does this matter beyond the visuals? These kinds of plots often appears when studying the (complex) eigenvalues of a real matrix that depends on a real parameter. For example, consider the matrix
\[M(\mu) = \begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1+\mu \\
1-\mu & 0
\end{bmatrix}\]
for real \(\mu\).
The eigenvalues \(\lambda\) of \(M\) satisify the equation \(\mu^2 + \lambda^2 = 1.\) Letting \(\mu = x\) and \(\lambda = y+zi\) recovers the plot of \(x^2 + (y+iz)^2 = 1.\)
From the geometry of the plot, we can immediately read off the eigenvalue behavior:
\[\begin{align*}
\mu < -1&: M(\mu) \text{ complex conjugate eigenvalues} \\
\mu = -1&: M(\mu) \text{ repeated eigenvalue } \lambda = 0 \\
-1 < \mu < 1&: M(\mu) \text{ one }+\text{ve and one }-\text{ve real eigenvalue} \\
\mu = 1&:  M(\mu) \text{ repated eigenvalue } \lambda = 0 \\
\mu > 1&: M(\mu) \text{ complex conjugate eigenvalues}
\end{align*}\]
More examples
Consider the matrix
\[M(\mu) = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & \mu \\
1 & 1
\end{bmatrix}\]
and think about its eigenvalues as a function of \(\mu\).
When \(\mu=1\), \(M(\mu)\) is degenerate and so has a zero eigenvalue. When \(\mu=0\), \(M(\mu)\) is a shear matrix with only one eigenvalue \(\lambda = 1\). As
shear matrices live on the boundary of diagonalisable and non-diagonalisable matrices
, we can reasonably further guess that if \(\mu<0\) then \(M(\mu)\) has complex conjugate eigenvalues and if \(\mu>0\) then \(M(\mu)\) has real eigenvalues.
Concretely, considering the eigenvalue equation \(\lambda^2 - 2\lambda + (1-\mu) = 0\) and letting \(\mu=x\) and \(\lambda=y+zi\) and re-arranging terms we get
\[\left((y+zi)-1\right)^2=x.\]
By splitting into real parts and imaginary parts and re-arranging terms we get
\[\begin{align*}
&\text{Real Part:} &(y-1)^2 - z^2 &= x, \\
&\text{Imaginary Part:} &(y-1)z &= 0.
\end{align*}\]
Again we have two cases
\[\begin{align*}
\text{Case 1: }y&=1 \text{ and so } -z^2 = x\\
\text{Case 2: }z&=0 \text{ and so } (y-1)^2 = 0
\end{align*}\]
Case 1 nets us a parabola in the \(xz\)-plane while Case 2 nets us a parabola in the \(xy\)-plane. Finally, we arrive at
the plot
.
You can create these sort of plots for any other 2 by 2 matrix that depends on one real parameter using
a desmos calculator
I made.

data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“雏鸡筛选”及其伦理和实际影响的讨论

不同观点：
• ZFleck：认为雏鸡筛选是不对的，尤其是看到小鸡被直接倒入绞肉机的场景让人难以接受。虽然肉类行业仍存在很多问题，但这一做法至少解决了一个。
• Maskawanian：对该做法持怀疑态度，认为这可能是行业为了效率而进行的“营销烟雾弹”，而非真正的伦理改进。他们指出，该做法并未解决雄性小鸡被杀的问题。
• Setgree：提出一个思想实验，询问如果自己是鸡，会选择立即死亡还是短暂的艰难生活，暗示雌性小鸡的生活质量值得质疑。
• Noa_buddy：指出公众对某些残酷行为的关注（如小鸡的碾压）与对常规农场动物的残酷行为（如吃肉和鸡蛋）的接受之间的矛盾。认为该做法在道德上至少对雄性小鸡是积极的，但不明确如果该做法扩大后是否仍然道德。
• Tantalor：质疑孵化前后杀死小鸡的伦理标准是否合理。
• Nemomarx：提到该技术在欧洲已有相当市场份额，暗示技术已经相对成熟。

补充讨论：
• Ndr：关注检测过程的技术细节，询问是否有影响鸡蛋健康或营养的操作。
• Throwawaymaths：质疑消费者投票是否必要，认为生产者可能乐于通过此方法节省成本。
• Bethekidyouwant：指出人类自古以来就选择性杀死雄性小鸡，并质疑雌性小鸡的生活质量是否真的好。
• Monster_truck：质疑有关美国每年扑杀数十亿雄性小鸡的数据准确性。
• Ada1981：认为雌性小鸡的生活同样痛苦，建议完全素食以解决伦理问题。
• XorNot：提出是否可以通过基因编辑技术（如CRISPR）来培育只产雌性鸡蛋的鸡，以节省成本。

争议焦点：
1. 雏鸡筛选是否真正提高了行业伦理标准，还是仅为效率服务。
2. 孵化前后杀死小鸡的伦理差异。
3. 如果该技术扩大应用，是否会对雌性小鸡的生活条件产生负面影响。
4. 数据准确性以及消费者和生产者在技术采用中的角色。

总结：讨论围绕雏鸡筛选的伦理性和实际影响展开，观点多样，从对具体操作的质疑到对整个肉类和蛋品行业的广泛批评。技术进步和伦理改进的平衡是争议的核心。

• Maskawanian：对该做法持怀疑态度，认为这可能是行业为了效率而进行的“营销烟雾弹”，而非真正的伦理改进。他们指出，该做法并未解决雄性小鸡被杀的问题。
• Setgree：提出一个思想实验，询问如果自己是鸡，会选择立即死亡还是短暂的艰难生活，暗示雌性小鸡的生活质量值得质疑。
• Noa_buddy：指出公众对某些残酷行为的关注（如小鸡的碾压）与对常规农场动物的残酷行为（如吃肉和鸡蛋）的接受之间的矛盾。认为该做法在道德上至少对雄性小鸡是积极的，但不明确如果该做法扩大后是否仍然道德。
• Tantalor：质疑孵化前后杀死小鸡的伦理标准是否合理。
• Nemomarx：提到该技术在欧洲已有相当市场份额，暗示技术已经相对成熟。

补充讨论：
• Ndr：关注检测过程的技术细节，询问是否有影响鸡蛋健康或营养的操作。
• Throwawaymaths：质疑消费者投票是否必要，认为生产者可能乐于通过此方法节省成本。
• Bethekidyouwant：指出人类自古以来就选择性杀死雄性小鸡，并质疑雌性小鸡的生活质量是否真的好。
• Monster_truck：质疑有关美国每年扑杀数十亿雄性小鸡的数据准确性。
• Ada1981：认为雌性小鸡的生活同样痛苦，建议完全素食以解决伦理问题。
• XorNot：提出是否可以通过基因编辑技术（如CRISPR）来培育只产雌性鸡蛋的鸡，以节省成本。

争议焦点：
1. 雏鸡筛选是否真正提高了行业伦理标准，还是仅为效率服务。
2. 孵化前后杀死小鸡的伦理差异。
3. 如果该技术扩大应用，是否会对雌性小鸡的生活条件产生负面影响。
4. 数据准确性以及消费者和生产者在技术采用中的角色。

总结：讨论围绕雏鸡筛选的伦理性和实际影响展开，观点多样，从对具体操作的质疑到对整个肉类和蛋品行业的广泛批评。技术进步和伦理改进的平衡是争议的核心。

主要讨论点：对Windows子系统 for Linux（WSL）的评价与使用体验

不同观点：
• 支持WSL的观点：
   - 认为WSL很有用，特别是在Windows环境中需要使用Linux工具时，WSL提供了一个便捷的方式。
   - 举例说明WSL在处理跨平台开发和脚本运行方面的高效性，比如在Windows上无缝运行Bash和Linux二进制文件。
   - 强调WSL 2的性能改进，特别是I/O性能提升，使其更具实用性。

• 批评WSL的观点：
   - 认为WSL存在一些限制和问题，比如与原生Linux环境的兼容性不足。
   - 指出WSL 2虽然有性能提升，但仍然无法完全替代完整的Linux虚拟机，尤其是在需要完整Linux内核特性时。
   - 举例说明某些Linux应用程序在WSL上运行不稳定或出现意外错误。

• 对WSL安全性与稳定性的担忧：
   - 有评论指出WSL可能带来安全风险，特别是在处理敏感数据或需要高安全性环境时。
   - 有人担心WSL的长期维护和支持问题，担心微软可能不会长期投入资源更新和维护WSL。

补充讨论：
• WSL与虚拟机的比较：
   - 一些用户认为WSL不能完全替代虚拟机，特别是在需要完全隔离的Linux环境时。
   - 另一方观点则认为WSL提供了虚拟机无法比拟的轻量级和集成度，特别适合快速开发和测试。

• WSL版本差异：
   - 讨论中提到WSL 1和WSL 2之间的差异，WSL 2被认为在性能和兼容性上更接近真实Linux环境。
   - 有用户建议根据具体需求选择WSL版本，以获得最佳体验。

争议焦点：
• WSL是否能真正替代传统的Linux虚拟机或双系统启动方案。
• WSL在安全性、稳定性和兼容性方面的表现是否足够可靠，以满足专业开发者的需求。

data.title: XML Summer School, Oxford. 14th to 19th Sept 2025
data.author: adamretter
data.article_summary: XML Summer School将于2025年9月14日至19日在牛津的圣艾德蒙学堂举办，庆祝其25周年。该活动面向使用、设计或实施XML及相关技术的人员，提供从XML基础到高级主题（如链接数据、网页设计和出版）的课程。教学形式包括小班授课、问答和实践环节，还有小组讨论和社交活动。初学者需从“XML入门课程”开始，其他课程要求具备基础知识。活动费用包含住宿、餐饮和社交活动，场地为历史悠久的圣艾德蒙学堂。如有课程选择疑问，可联系主办方咨询。更多信息和照片可在Flickr group或相关主题标签（如#xmlss25）查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个因访问量增加而达到资源限制的网站链接的多种反应和讨论，包括对XML、XSLT及相关技术的历史回顾、技术问题以及道德争议。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与历史视角] duncans 表示对2000-2001年间XML和XSLT以及语义网技术的怀念，并对这些技术在近十年后仍被认真对待感到惊讶，还提到相关活动至今仍在举办，并表达了祝福。

• [技术问题] NohatCoder 关注网站因使用IOMART的云服务、并在一些用户点击链接后停止工作的问题，认为这是不令人印象深刻的技术表现。

• [流行趋势] radiator 简单提到XML目前在Hacker News（HN）上非常流行，暗示该技术仍有一定的关注度。

• [个人经历与幽默] petesergeant 以幽默的语气提到自己曾因大学计算机系的缘故编写了“非常疯狂的XML”，并分享了相关代码链接，同时提到即将去牛津参加活动。

• [道德质疑] olalonde 对整个情况表示了某种道德上的质疑，但没有详细阐述具体质疑的内容。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中有人提到了对XML和XSLT等技术的怀旧情绪，显示出这些技术在过去的影响力以及其持续的生命力。
• 有人指出了技术实现上的不足，特别是在处理流量突增时的表现。
• 道德上的质疑虽然没有详细说明，但可能涉及到对技术资源使用或活动本身的一些伦理考虑。

争议焦点：主要集中在技术实现的可靠性和对活动或技术使用上的道德评价。

44635187.article_content:
The XML Summer School is back at St Edmund Hall for 2025!
Sunday 14th to Friday 19th September
Register Now
Join us in Oxford to celebrate 25 years of the XML Summer School!
What is the XML Summer School?
The XML Summer School is a unique event for everyone using, designing, or implementing solutions using XML and related technologies, held in Oxford, UK. The week-long event is made up of courses which range from the basics of XML to advanced topics in linked data, web design, and publishing. Faculty tutors include practitioners and academics who are at the forefront of XML and related technologies.
How is the teaching structured?
Each course comprises a series of small-group classes, with plenty of time for questions and discussion. Some courses also feature a hands-on component, where you’ll have the opportunity to try out the techniques you have learned, and receive feedback and support on your work. There are also panel discussions, and informal learning opportunities over meals and evening activities.
What prior knowledge do I need?
That depends. The Hands-on Introduction to XML course is intended for anyone who needs to work with XML and wants to learn the basics. The other courses all assume at least this basic level of knowledge, so if you’re a beginner, you’ll need to take the Hands-on Introduction before moving on to the more advanced training. If you’re unsure about the suitability of any of our courses for your specific needs, please get in touch and we’ll be happy to advise you!
What about accommodation and meals?
Accommodation, meals, and social events are included in the fee. The venue is St Edmund Hall, one of the most historic sites at the University of Oxford, dating back to the 12th century. All the faculty and delegates stay in college and take part in the social events, so there’s lots of opportunity to discuss questions that arise after the classes. The
XML Summer School Flickr group
has photos of the college as well as sessions and events. Or you can search for the hashtags we’ve used in the past (
#xmlssxx
, where
#xmlsummerschoolxx
, where
xx
is the two-digit year).

Treasury Secretary Bessent: Need to examine whether the Fed as an institution has been successful
Squawk Box
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday suggested a review of the Federal Reserve that would go beyond the current controversy over building renovations and look at its overall function.
"What we need to do is examine the entire Federal Reserve institution and whether they have been successful," Bessent said during an interview on CNBC's "
Squawk Box
." "Has the organization succeeded in its mission? If this were the [Federal Aviation Administration] and we were having this many mistakes, we would go back and look at why has this happened."
The comments come amid
an intensifying conflict
between the White House and the central bank. It was not clear what form a review would take or who would perform it.
Last week saw conflicting reports over whether President
Donald Trump
was preparing to fire Fed Chair
Jerome Powell
. Reports from the White House indicated
a move was forthcoming
, but Trump soon after denied he is readying what would be a legally questionable maneuver.
Bessent has been at the center of the controversy, both as
a potential successor
at the Fed as well as reports pointing to the Treasury chief as a mediator looking to discourage Trump from ousting Powell.
"President Trump solicits a whole range of opinions and then makes a decision," Bessent said when asked about
a Wall Street Journal report
that he had helped convince Trump to stay his hand on Powell. "So he takes a lot of inputs, and at the end of the day it's his decision."
Trump
has demanded the Fed
dramatically lower its benchmark overnight borrowing rate, something that appears unlikely regardless of the chair.
In addition, the administration in recent days has criticized the Fed for
cost overruns
at the $2.5 billion renovation it has undertaken for two of its buildings in Washington. Administration officials reportedly are planning soon to view the project in person.
On the question of interest rates, Bessent backed the idea that the Fed probably should be easing with inflation mostly moderating.
"They were fear mongering over tariffs, and thus far we have seen very little, if any, inflation," Bessent said. "We've had great inflation numbers. So, you know, I think this idea [is] of them not being able to break out of a certain mindset. All these Ph.D.s over there, I don't know what they do."
The Fed last cut rates in December, which completed a brief easing cycle that brought the fed funds rate down a full percentage point. However, as the Fed eased both mortgage rates and Treasury yields moved higher.
Market pricing indicates the Fed probably will cut again in September.

data.title: Liquid Glass Design or Kitsch?
data.author: samsolomon
data.article_summary: Apple推出了名为“Liquid Glass”的全新设计语言，旨在统一其所有操作系统（iOS、iPadOS、macOS、tvOS、watchOS）的用户界面。该设计看起来新鲜、动态，并保持了品牌一致性，但也面临一些挑战。新设计引发了网上褒贬不一的反应，尽管名字不太理想，但其动画和概念显得大胆创新。然而，在不同设备上的效果有所不同，特别是在macOS上，透明度效果可能并不总是提升用户体验。此外，过多的视觉效果可能影响可读性和能耗，初版设计因效果过多而功能不足，后续进行了调整。文章质疑Liquid Glass究竟是优秀设计还是流于俗套（kitsch），认为目前版本介于两者之间，但正朝着正确方向发展。整体而言，Apple的统一设计具有潜力，但仍需解决技术问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对不同主题的分析与评价，包括体育摄影、社交媒体反馈、iOS 26设计以及设计与可用性的关系。

不同观点：
• PaulHoule讨论了体育摄影的挑战，指出从体育比赛中捕捉具有清晰故事性的画面非常困难。他提到普通画面无法明确讲述故事，例如篮球比赛中谁得分。他还分享了一次拍摄掷铁饼的经历，认为虽然受保护网影响画面，但好的体育照片可以通过特殊角度捕捉关键时刻，例如棒球比赛中的紧张瞬间。

• eviks对社交媒体上的反馈进行了批评，认为一些反馈缺乏意义，像 carnival music（狂欢音乐）一样嘈杂且可预测。他们指出可读性是一个值得关注的问题，并认为PaulHoule忽略了这一点，尽管提供了截图和录音作为支持。

• Svoka对iOS 26的设计表示赞赏，认为新设计使得操作更加简便和现代化，特别是对开发者而言功能性更强。不过，他们认为将设计焦点放在“glass”组件上是狭隘且肤浅的，整体布局的改革才是关键。

• recursivedoubts批评了设计中的创新趋势，认为这些创新往往牺牲了可用性，变成了一种时尚。他们指出管理层试图通过这种“创新”来推动升级周期，但没有提供视觉例子来支持他们的观点。

补充讨论：
• PaulHoule与eviks之间存在对反馈质量的争议，前者强调摄影艺术性，后者则关注反馈中的可读性问题。
• Svoka和recursivedoubts对于新设计的态度截然不同，前者欣赏新设计的现代化和功能性改进，而后者则批评设计创新忽略了可用性。

Design or Kitsch?

4 minute READ
Apple has unveiled a bold new design language for all its operating systems. It’s still too early to say how good or bad it is, but we can outline the challenges.
It looks fresh, dynamic, and (very) on-brand. The fact that iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS now all follow the same UI patterns is good news, and we can only imagine how hard it was to coordinate and push through in a huge organization like Apple.
First Impressions
As expected, Apple’s announcement triggered the usual flood of sarcasm and glee online. Of course, it’s not all bad. Some of the world’s best designers worked on this… and designers, being human, make mistakes.
The backlash after Apple launches something new has become tradition. It’s as loud as it is predictable, and the insight you get from first reactions on Social Media is as meaningful as any carnival music.
Let’s be honest:
Liquid Glass
isn’t a great name. But the concept is bold, the animations feel fresh, and apps still using the previous look already seem a step behind.
More importantly, this shift isn’t just cosmetic. It’s the first time Apple has introduced a truly unified design across all platforms. UI elements render live and morph with context. That’s not just aesthetic polish. It’s systemic change.
The Metaphor
As a metaphor, glass is consistent and logical on
iPhone
, a device made of glass with limited surface area. No matter the model, space is always tight.
Glass works similarly on
iPad
, where the interface is also defined by touching a glass screen. But it’s arguably less necessary here, since the iPad has, broadly speaking, enough space for simultaneous UI.
Remember Aqua, Apple’s major OS redesign from 25 years ago? Aqua means “water,” which acts like a form of “liquid glass.” So while there are roots going back decades, which is nice, that history makes Liquid Glass feel less fresh and a little less convincing on
macOS
, which otherwise has just become a lot rounder.
Where Liquid Glass Works… and Where It Doesn’t
Looking at Liquid Glass on macOS raises the question of whether transparency should be limited to contexts where it clearly improves the experience. Liquid Glass seems helpful on smaller devices. On iPad and macOS, it may make sense in situations where:
There is limited space or UI elements get in the way
Controls appear on time-limited UI elements where readability isn’t a concern, like media player controls
Transparency improves clarity; like play buttons on videos, contextual menus on photos, or secondary text
Moving forward, Apple might consider keeping the full-on glass effect time-limited. Visual effects have the most impact when used sparingly. Think of the spectacular Siri wave or Apple Intelligence animations. They surprise and delight precisely because they appear and vanish.
The Laocoön-effect
Liquid Glass may suffer from a Laocoön effect:
1
According to Lessing, dynamic action forced into a static medium distorts or diminishes the intended expression. Glass is a static material, and animating glass is inaccurate.
But it looks great…like the Siri wave or Apple Intelligence effects. What’s not to like? Mind you, good design is not primarily about aesthetics. The question is whether Liquid Glass works.
Readability is a concern. So is energy consumption. And visually, the overall look feels blurred. Some quick app icon renders appear smudged: a surprising waste on such a crisp screen. Maybe it just takes some getting used to, but the icons are neither circles nor squares, which gives them an odd, undecided feel.
In fact, the first iteration didn’t work too well. Too much effect, not enough function. So they toned it down. Does it work now? Or is it still trying to be something it’s not?
2
“Desire lacking ability turns to Kitsch.” —Jan Tschichold
3
So this is the ultimate dare for a company known for world-class design. Liquid Glass: does it work, or is it kitsch?
Potential
Glass as an Extension of the Device
Using glass as an extension of the screen makes sense. It might be more convincing if glass elements didn’t float independently below the surface, made of glass. But they worked with the surface. If the glass we interact with was working with the glass we touch. Like the fake click effect, some UI elements could be rendered to feel like a dynamic indentation on the surface you touch.
Imagine a form field that looks and feels like your phone’s screen has a real indent. If the glass effect is tied directly to the surface interaction, the animation would feel consistent… and the Laocoön-effect wouldn’t be a concern.
Design or Kitsch?
So, is it design or kitsch? The first beta leaned toward the kitschy side. It didn’t quite work. Right now, it’s somewhere in between, but heading in the right direction. The better it works, the less it’s just effect, the more it becomes design.

44634711.article_summary: Apple推出了名为“Liquid Glass”的全新设计语言，旨在统一其所有操作系统（iOS、iPadOS、macOS、tvOS、watchOS）的用户界面。该设计看起来新鲜、动态，并保持了品牌一致性，但也面临一些挑战。新设计引发了网上褒贬不一的反应，尽管名字不太理想，但其动画和概念显得大胆创新。然而，在不同设备上的效果有所不同，特别是在macOS上，透明度效果可能并不总是提升用户体验。此外，过多的视觉效果可能影响可读性和能耗，初版设计因效果过多而功能不足，后续进行了调整。文章质疑Liquid Glass究竟是优秀设计还是流于俗套（kitsch），认为目前版本介于两者之间，但正朝着正确方向发展。整体而言，Apple的统一设计具有潜力，但仍需解决技术问题。

data.article_summary: "Perfect is the enemy of good"是一句常归因于伏尔泰的格言，意指对完美的过度追求往往阻碍了良好改进的实现。该短语强调，追求绝对完美可能不切实际，不应让对完美的执着妨碍对虽不完美但仍有价值的事物的欣赏或执行。这一理念可追溯至亚里士多德等古典哲学家的"中庸之道"原则，并在莎士比亚等文学作品中有所体现。现代应用包括计算机优化领域中唐纳德·克努斯的“过早优化是万恶之源”等观点。该概念也出现在市场营销中的“质量蠕变”现象，强调过度追求完美可能适得其反。

44633745.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
For the album, see
Rhys Muldoon
.
Aphorism commonly attributed to Voltaire
"
Perfect is the enemy of good
" is an
aphorism
that means insistence on perfection often prevents implementation of good improvements. The phrase argues that achieving absolute
perfection
may be impossible; one should not let the struggle for perfection stand in the way of appreciating or executing on something that is imperfect but still meritable.
Origin
[
edit
]
In the English-speaking world the aphorism is commonly attributed to
Voltaire
, who quoted an Italian
proverb
in his
Questions sur l'Encyclopédie
in 1770: "
Il meglio è l'inimico del bene
".
[
1
]
It subsequently appeared in his
moral
poem,
La Bégueule
, which starts:
[
2
]
Dans ses écrits, un sage Italien
Dit que le mieux est l'ennemi du bien.
In his writings, a wise Italian
says that the best is the enemy of the good.
Previously, around 1726, in his
Pensées
,
Montesquieu
wrote "
Le mieux est le mortel ennemi du bien
" ('The best is the mortal enemy of the good').
[
3
]
Antecedents
[
edit
]
Aristotle
and other classical philosophers propounded the principle of the
golden mean
which counsels against
extremism
in general.
[
4
]
Its sense in English literature can be traced back to
Shakespeare
.
[
5
]
In his tragedy
King Lear
(1606), the
Duke of Albany
warns of "striving to better, oft we mar what's well" and in
Sonnet 103
:
Were it not sinful then, striving to mend,
To mar the subject that before was well?
Variations
[
edit
]
The 1893
Dictionary of Quotations from Ancient and Modern, English and Foreign Sources
lists a similar proverb, which it claims is of
Chinese
provenance: "Better a
diamond
with a flaw than a pebble without one".
More recent applications include
Robert Watson-Watt
propounding a "cult of the imperfect", which he stated as "Give them the third best to go on with; the second best comes too late, the best never comes";
[
6
]
economist
George Stigler
's assertion that "If you never miss a plane, you're spending too much time at the airport";
[
7
]
[
8
]
and, in the field of
computer program optimization
,
Donald Knuth
's statement that "Premature optimization is the root of all evil".
[
9
]
In marketing, the concept of "quality creep" is also recognised as counterproductive.
[
10
]
See also
[
edit
]
Gold plating (software engineering)
If it ain't broke, don't fix it
Nirvana fallacy
Satisficing
Utopia
Wabi-sabi
Worse is better
KISS Principle

[
edit
]

. Vol. 2. Geneva, Switzerland: (publisher not named). p. 250.
^

;

; Hugh Barr Nisbet (1991),

主要讨论点：围绕美国政治中"建制派"与"反建制派"的争论，以及对具体政客如米奇·麦康奈尔（Mitch McConnell）的评价。

不同观点：
• **支持反建制派的观点**：
  - 认为建制派的政客，如米奇·麦康奈尔，长期占据权力位置但并未带来真正的变革。
  - 反建制派的崛起是对传统政治精英的反抗，旨在打破现有的政治僵局。
  - 例子：提到茶党运动和特朗普的崛起，认为这是民众对建制派不满的体现。

• **支持建制派的观点**：
  - 认为建制派政客拥有丰富的经验和政治资源，能在复杂的政治环境中推动政策。
  - 反建制派虽然有活力，但缺乏实际的政治操作经验，可能导致政策不稳定。
  - 例子：指出米奇·麦康奈尔在参议院的领导地位帮助共和党实现了一些关键立法胜利。

• **对米奇·麦康奈尔个人评价的争议**：
  - 有人批评麦康奈尔是典型的建制派代表，过于注重权力维护而忽视民众需求。
  - 也有人认为他在复杂的政治环境中表现出了高超的策略能力，对共和党有实质性贡献。
  - 争议焦点：麦康奈尔是否真正为选民服务，还是只关心自己的政治地位。

• **对反建制派运动可持续性的讨论**：
  - 有人质疑反建制派运动是否能长久持续，担心其缺乏明确的政策纲领和组织结构。
  - 支持者认为反建制派的活力和草根特性正是其优势，能够更灵活地回应选民需求。

补充讨论：
- **茶党运动和特朗普影响**：评论中多次提到茶党运动和特朗普，作为反建制派崛起的标志性事件。
- **政治策略和妥协**：有评论指出，建制派和反建制派在政治策略上的不同，前者更倾向于妥协和渐进改革，而后者更激进。
- **选民基础**：讨论了不同政治派别背后的选民基础及其诉求，强调了选民对政治精英的不满情绪。

这些观点展示了美国政治中建制派与反建制派之间的复杂互动，以及对具体政客评价的多样性。争议的焦点主要集中在政治精英的角色及其对选民的实际影响上。

data.title: OpenAI claims gold-medal performance at IMO 2025
data.author: Davidzheng
data.article_summary: 本文简要指出，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致在x.com网站上出现问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过此方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI在国际数学奥林匹克（IMO）问题上取得的突破及其意义

不同观点：
• [og_kalu] 认为该成果是OpenAI一个小团队在近期开发的新技术基础上实现的，甚至对OpenAI的许多研究人员来说也是个惊喜。这表明AI在前沿能力上的进展非常迅速。
• [rafael859] 指出，解决这些数学问题的证明使用了有限的词汇，并调侃这种简洁的表达方式。同时提到Alex Wei是国际信息学奥林匹克（IOI）的金牌得主，暗示其个人能力对成果的贡献。
• [tlb] 强调这些数学问题非常困难，鼓励那些认为这些问题简单的人亲自尝试解决。
• [hislaziness] 引用了著名数学家陶哲轩（Terence Tao）对此事的看法，但没有具体说明其立场。
• [gniv] 指出模型解决了问题P1到P5，但未能解决最难的P6问题，这与人类选手的情况类似。
• [dylanbyte] 认为这些问题仅在背景知识上属于高中水平，但难度极高。专业数学家除非有IMO背景，否则也难以达到这种表现。这并不意味着模型在数学上优于人类，而是因为数学家的专长在于拓展数学的前沿。

补充讨论：
• [demirbey05] 提到谷歌也在IMO上取得了金奖，并暗示OpenAI可能通过大量投入计算资源取得成果。还提到最近的一份报告评估了LLM在IMO 2025上的表现，显示o3高分未获得铜牌。
• [modeless] 引用Noam Brown的观点，指出该模型并非专门针对IMO问题，而是一个通用的推理模型，且具有提升效率的潜力。还提到AI在科学发现中的贡献可能即将到来。
• [johnecheck] 对OpenAI的具体方法表示好奇，怀疑是否通过大规模并行运行模型并选择最佳结果来实现，认为这可能降低成果的令人兴奋程度。
• [meroes] 认为在强化学习与人类反馈（RLHF）领域中，AI公司聘用IMO选手可能对进展有贡献，因此难以判断此成果的真正意义。
• [z7] 提到之前的预测，包括Paul Christiano和Eliezer Yudkowsky对IMO挑战的看法，认为这一成果可能对AI风险评估有重要影响。
• [quirino] 强调OpenAI团队在AtCoder World Tour Finals 2025上的表现同样 impressive，指出其在编程竞赛中仅次于一名人类选手。

争议焦点：
• OpenAI是否通过大量计算资源投入（如并行运行模型多次）来取得这一成果，以及这是否会影响成果的实际意义。
• 该模型是否真的具有通用性，还是仅在特定任务上有优异表现。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 该成果对AI在科学发现中的潜在贡献及其未来发展趋势的影响。
• 不同背景的人对IMO问题难度和AI表现的理解差异。

data.title: Jqfmt like gofmt, but for jq
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: `jqfmt` 是一个类似于 `gofmt` 的工具，专门用于格式化 `jq` 命令行脚本。它帮助用户在阅读或编写复杂的 `jq` 查询时，通过在适当位置添加换行符来提高可读性。开发者因经常处理包含大量 `jq` 的 Shell 单行脚本，创建了 `jqfmt` 来解决格式问题。该工具支持格式化数组、对象以及操作符，并提供了命令行选项来定制输出格式。尽管最初依赖 `gojq`，但由于其无法提供可遍历的语法树，开发者自行提取了相关代码。`jqfmt` 以 MIT 协议开源，并欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕工具 **jq** 及其相关工具（如 **jqfmt**）的讨论，包括使用体验、优缺点以及替代方案。

不同观点：
• **支持并分享使用经验**：[rwiggins] 对 jq 有很高的评价，并分享了自己常用的一个 jq 单行命令来分析文档结构，同时对 jqfmt 工具进行了测试和反馈，认为其格式化功能不错，但希望有些默认行为可以改进。

• **澄清误解**：[Hendrikto] 指出 "jq formatter" 在搜索时容易引起误解，因为 jq 本身可以格式化命令，而不是直接格式化 JSON 数据，帮助读者更好理解讨论背景。

• **质疑单行命令的复杂性**：[s17n] 认为如果需要格式化单行命令，可能它就不应该被写成单行，暗示 jq 命令有时过于复杂，对工具的存在表示一定质疑，但仍认可工具的创新性。

• **对工具默认设置的建议**：[kiitos] 建议 jqfmt 工具应该默认启用一些常用格式化规则，而不是让用户手动启用每一个规则，从而提升用户体验。

• **对 jq 的批评和使用困难**：[xmonkee] 表示不喜欢 jq，认为其命令难以记忆和使用，且文档难以理解。每年仅使用一次，但每次都需要重新学习，暗示工具的学习曲线陡峭。

• **替代工具推荐**：[mikeocool] 提到最近使用 fx (fx.wtf) 作为 jq 的替代工具，提供类似 JavaScript 的接口，可以完成类似 jq 的处理任务。

• **幽默评论**：[guerrilla] 以幽默方式表示对标题的误解，增加了一些轻松的讨论氛围。

• **工具作者回应及推广**：[noperator] 作为 jqfmt 工具的作者，回应了讨论，并推广了自己开发的另一个工具 sol，用于 shell 单行命令的美化。

• **对命名和工具类比的批评**：[ForOldHack] 对工具命名提出了批评，认为类似 jq、gofmt、jqfmt 这些工具的命名方式容易混淆，并表达了对老式设备的怀念。

• **jq 在复杂任务中的局限性**：[quotemstr] 认为 jq 在处理大数据集的复杂任务时表现不佳，尤其是与 Python 和 Pandas 等工具相比，运行速度较慢，暗示在某些情况下应选择更强大的工具。

补充讨论：
• jq 的复杂性和学习曲线是争议的焦点，部分用户认为其命令难以记忆和使用，而另一部分用户则高度评价其功能和灵活性。
• 关于 jqfmt 工具的反馈主要集中在其默认行为和易用性上，部分用户希望能有更简便的使用体验。
• 替代工具如 fx 被提出，显示出用户对 jq 以外的选择也持有开放态度。
